erdos-0012.statement: Call an infinite $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ admissible if no distinct $a,b,c\in A$ satisfy $a<b$, $a<c$ and $a\mid b+c$. Three questions: (i) can an admissible $A$ have $\liminf_{N\to\infty}|A\cap[1,N]|/\sqrt N>0$? (ii) is there an absolute $c>0$ such that every admissible $A$ has $|A\cap[1,N]|<N^{1-c}$ for infinitely many $N$? (iii) must $\sum_{n\in A}1/n$ converge for every admissible $A$?

hilbert-08.category_rationale: Hilbert 8 bundles RH, Goldbach, twin primes, prime solutions of ax+by+c=0 and a number-field transfer. The transfer is answered only at the prime-number-theorem level (Landau 1903; Hecke); its RH-level form (extended RH for Dedekind zeta functions) is open, so no named part has an accepted complete answer. The other parts are open.

If read as asking for a non-abelian reciprocity law, it is open (Langlands program).

hilbert-09.statement: Find the most general reciprocity law in an arbitrary algebraic number field. (Hilbert's text asks for the law of $l$-th power residues for $l$ an odd prime, a power of $2$ or a power of an odd prime; modern accounts read the problem as asking for a general, including non-abelian, reciprocity law.)

wps-039.status_headline: Solved. Bourgain, Demeter and Guth (2015; Annals 2016) proved it for degree above three by decoupling; Wooley settled the cubic case.
wps-039.verifier_checks: Crossref: Annals 184(2) 633-682 (2016-09-01, "for degrees higher than three"); Adv. Math. 294 532-561 (Wooley, cubic case); arXiv 1512.01565v3. The statement J_{s,k}(X) << X^eps(X^s + X^{2s-k(k+1)/2}) is correct; k>=4 (BDG) plus k=3 (Wooley) plus the classical k<=2 cases give the full main conjecture. S2 holds.

wps-040.statement: For every $d\ge1$, is there a constant $c(d)$ such that every $d$-degenerate graph $H$ has Ramsey number $R(H)\le c(d)\,|V(H)|$?

wps-041.statement: Can the positive integers be split into two classes so that no class contains a Pythagorean triple $(a,b,c)$ with $a^2+b^2=c^2$?

wps-042.name: Sensitivity conjecture
wps-042.statement: Is there an absolute constant $C$ such that every Boolean function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ satisfies $\deg(f)\le s(f)^{C}$ (equivalently $bs(f)\le s(f)^C$), where $s$ is sensitivity, $bs$ block sensitivity and $\deg$ real polynomial degree?

statement_sources.label: Huang, Induced subgraphs of hypercubes and a proof of the Sensitivity Conjecture (Annals 2019)

wps-042.status_headline: Solved (true). Hao Huang (2019, Annals of Mathematics) showed every induced subgraph on 2^{n-1}+1 hypercube vertices has max degree >= sqrt(n), giving deg(f) <= s(f)^2.
wps-042.verifier_checks: Crossref: Annals 190(3) 949-955 (2019-11); arXiv 1907.00847v2 abstract. Statement (deg <= s^C, equivalently bs <= s^C) accurate. S2 holds.

wps-043.statement: Is the Conway knot ($11n34$) smoothly slice, i.e. does it bound a smoothly, properly embedded disk in the 4-ball $B^4$?

wpu-000.category_rationale: Known up to the 2-part for all totally real fields (via Wiles's proof of the main conjecture for odd p) and completely for abelian fields (2-part via Rognes–Weibel with Kolster); the general 2-part rests on a 2-adic main conjecture (Kolster 1989) not found proved.

evidence.note: Survey of K_2 of fields including special values of zeta functions and the Birch–Tate relation.
evidence.title: Some aspects of the functor K_2 of fields

evidence.note: Shows that Fédérer's proposed 2-adic main conjecture for totally real fields would imply the 2-primary part of Birch–Tate (a conditional result).
evidence.title: A relation between the 2-primary parts of the main conjecture and the Birch–Tate conjecture

evidence.claimant: J. Rognes, C. Weibel (appendix by M. Kolster)
evidence.note: Relates 2-primary K-theory of rings of integers to étale cohomology and zeta values; for totally real abelian fields this yields the 2-part of Birch–Tate.
evidence.title: Two-primary algebraic K-theory of rings of integers in number fields

wpu-000.name: Birch–Tate conjecture

partial_results.text: For totally real abelian number fields the 2-primary part of the conjecture holds, completing the abelian case.
partial_results.title: 2-part for abelian fields (Rognes–Weibel, appendix by Kolster)

wpu-000.review_reason: Status of the 2-primary part for non-abelian totally real fields not verified; recent work on 2-adic main conjectures or the Brumer–Stark conjecture over Z could settle it, which would make the conjecture fully proved. Check an expert source.
wpu-000.statement: For a totally real number field $F$ with ring of integers $\mathcal O_F$, let $w_2(F)$ be the largest integer $N$ such that $\mathrm{Gal}(F(\mu_N)/F)$ has exponent dividing $2$. The Birch–Tate conjecture asserts $\#K_2(\mathcal O_F)=\lvert w_2(F)\,\zeta_F(-1)\rvert$, where $K_2(\mathcal O_F)$ is the (finite) tame kernel, i.e. the centre of the Steinberg group of $\mathcal O_F$.

statement_sources.label: Dalawat, Some aspects of the functor K_2 of fields, J. Ramanujan Math. Soc. 21 (2006) (arXiv math/0311099)
Kolster, A relation between the 2-primary parts of the main conjecture and the Birch–Tate conjecture, Canad. Math. Bull. 32 (1989)

wpu-000.status_headline: Open only at the prime 2: proved for abelian fields and up to powers of 2 for all totally real fields via the Iwasawa main conjecture.
wpu-000.verifier_checks: Opened arXiv math/0311099v4 (Dalawat, JRMS 21 (2006)), the Kolster CMB 32 (1989) page, and the Crossref abstract for Rognes–Weibel JAMS 13 (2000) (zeta-function relation for totally real abelian F; 2-primary Lichtenbaum). So 'proved up to 2 for all totally real F, completely for abelian F' is consistent. I could not confirm the current status of the 2-part for non-abelian fields (web search budget exhausted; the arXiv search shows no 2025–26 paper claiming it). The statement shared an 8-word run with the Wikipedia article ('let F be a totally real number field') and was rewritten; the maths is

wpu-001.name: Casas-Alvero conjecture
wpu-001.statement: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic $0$ and $f\in K[x]$ monic of degree $d\ge1$. Suppose that for every $i=1,\dots,d-1$ the polynomials $f$ and $f^{(i)}$ (the $i$-th derivative) share a nonconstant common factor. Must $f=(x-a)^d$ for some $a\in K$? (The analogue fails in positive characteristic.)

statement_sources.label: Castryck–Laterveer–Ounaïes, Constraints on counterexamples to the Casas-Alvero conjecture (arXiv 1208.5404)

wpu-001.status_headline: Open. Ghosh (arXiv 2025, revised Mar 2026) claims a proof; not accepted. Known for degrees p^k, 2p^k and other special families.

wpu-002.name: Connes embedding problem
wpu-002.statement: Connes (1976): does every type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $M$ with separable predual admit a trace-preserving embedding into an ultrapower $\mathcal R^{\omega}$ of the hyperfinite $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $\mathcal R$? Equivalently, can the joint moments of every finite tuple of self-adjoint elements of $M$ be approximated arbitrarily well by those of matrices with the normalized trace?

statement_sources.label: Goldbring, The Connes embedding problem: a guided tour, Bull. AMS (2022)

wpu-002.status_headline: Solved (negative): the MIP* = RE theorem (Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright, Yuen, 2020) implies a non-embeddable II_1 factor exists; broadly accepted.

AMS 59(4) (2022), doi 10.1090/bull/1768 (says a negative solution was obtained via MIP*=RE), and the EMS Press page for Vidick's ICM 2022 chapter (published 2023-12-15, pp. 4996–5025). wpu-003.statement: Let $A,B$ be $n\times n$ complex normal matrices with eigenvalues $a_1,\dots,a_n$ and $b_1,\dots,b_n$. Marcus and de Oliveira conjectured that $\det(A+B)$ always lies in the convex hull of the $n!$ complex numbers $\prod_{i=1}^n\bigl(a_i+b_{\sigma(i)}\bigr)$, $\sigma\in S_n$.

wpu-004.name: Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture
wpu-004.statement: Let $G$ be a group with integral cohomological dimension $\mathrm{cd}\,G=2$. Must $G$ then have geometric dimension $2$, i.e. admit a $2$-dimensional CW complex as an Eilenberg–MacLane space $K(G,1)$? (Eilenberg and Ganea proved $\mathrm{gd}\,G=\mathrm{cd}\,G$ whenever $\mathrm{cd}\,G\ge3$, and $\mathrm{gd}\,G\le3$ when $\mathrm{cd}\,G=2$.)

partial_results.text: The K-theoretic conjecture holds for hyperbolic groups with coefficients in any associative ring.

wpu-005.statement: For every group $G$ and ring $R$, the Farrell–Jones conjecture asserts that the assembly maps $H^G_n(E_{\mathcal{VCyc}}G;\mathbf K_R)\to K_n(R[G])$ and $H^G_n(E_{\mathcal{VCyc}}G;\mathbf L^{\langle-\infty\rangle}_R)\to L^{\langle-\infty\rangle}_n(R[G])$ are isomorphisms for all $n\in\mathbb Z$, where $E_{\mathcal{VCyc}}G$ is the classifying space for the family of virtually cyclic subgroups. (The full version allows twisted coefficients and passes to finite wreath products.)

Lück–Reich, The Baum–Connes and the Farrell–Jones conjectures in K- and L-theory (arXiv math/0402405)

wpu-006.name: Bost conjecture
wpu-006.review_reason: Limited verification of current status (web search budget exhausted). The Wikipedia list calls it 'a specific case of the Farrell–Jones conjecture', but it is the ℓ¹-analogue of Baum–Connes (described in the FJ article); confirm how to present it.
wpu-006.statement: For a countable discrete group $G$, the Bost conjecture asserts that the $\ell^1$-assembly map $\mu_{\ell^1}\colon K^G_*(\underline{E}G)\to K_*(\ell^1(G))$, from the equivariant K-homology of the classifying space for proper actions to the topological K-theory of the Banach algebra $\ell^1(G)$, is an isomorphism. Composing with $K_*(\ell^1(G))\to K_*(C^*_r(G))$ gives the Baum–Connes assembly map.

statement_sources.label: Lück–Reich, The Baum–Connes and the Farrell–Jones conjectures in K- and L-theory (arXiv math/0402405)

By Pálfy and Pudlák (1980) this is equivalent to asking whether every finite lattice is isomorphic to an interval $[H,G]$ of the subgroup lattice of some finite group $G$.

wpu-008.name: Goncharov conjecture
wpu-008.review_reason: Check whether Kupers–Rudenko–Sierra (2026) or their companion paper settles the Γ_F(n) cohomology statement for number fields (a special case), and how far the weight-3 case is known.
wpu-008.statement: For a field $F$ and $n\ge2$, Goncharov defined, from higher Bloch groups $\mathcal B_k(F)$, a complex $\Gamma_F(n)$ in degrees $1,\dots,n$: $\mathcal B_n(F)\to\mathcal B_{n-1}(F)\otimes F^\times_{\mathbb Q}\to\cdots\to\Lambda^nF^\times_{\mathbb Q}$. He conjectured $H^i(\Gamma_F(n))\cong H^i_{\mathcal M}(F,\mathbb Q(n))$ for all $i$, i.e. the Adams-weight-$n$ part of $K_{2n-i}(F)\otimes\mathbb Q$.

statement_sources.label: Goncharov, Geometry of configurations, polylogarithms, and motivic cohomology, Adv. Math. 114 (1995)
Gangl, The Grassmannian complex and Goncharov's motivic complex in weight 4 (arXiv 1801.07816)

wpu-009.statement: Let $C$ be a smooth non-hyperelliptic complex projective curve of genus $g\ge3$, canonically embedded in $\mathbb{P}^{g-1}$, with Clifford index $\operatorname{Cliff}(C)$. Green (1984) conjectured that the Koszul cohomology groups satisfy $K_{p,2}(C,K_C)=0$ for every $p<\operatorname{Cliff}(C)$, so that the linear strand of the canonical resolution determines $\operatorname{Cliff}(C)$. The non-vanishing $K_{\operatorname{Cliff}(C),2}(C,K_C)\ne0$ is a theorem of Green and Lazarsfeld.

wpu-010.statement:
Let $X$ be a smooth variety over a number field $K$ and $(E,
abla)$ a vector bundle on $X$ with an integrable connection, spread out over a ring of $S$-integers. If for almost all primes $\mathfrak p$ the reduction of $(E,
abla)$ modulo $\mathfrak p$ has vanishing $p$-curvature, then $(E,
abla)$ should have finite monodromy, i.e. become trivial on a finite étale cover of $X_{ ar K}$ (the differential system has a full set of algebraic solutions).

wpu-013.statement: Let $D$ be a $(v,k,\lambda)$ difference set in an abelian group $G$ of order $v$, with order $n=k-\lambda$. Lander (1983) conjectured that whenever some prime $p$ divides $\gcd(v,n)$, the Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$ is non-cyclic. It implies Ryser's conjecture on cyclic difference sets and hence the circulant Hadamard conjecture.

wpu-014.statement: Ryser's circulant Hadamard conjecture (1963): call an $n\times n$ matrix circulant if each row is obtained from the row above by a cyclic shift of one place. If such a matrix $H$ has all entries $\pm1$ and satisfies $HH^{\mathsf T}=nI_n$, then $n\in\{1,4\}$; in other words, no circulant Hadamard matrix of order greater than $4$ exists.

wpu-015.statement: A Barker sequence of length $n$ is $a_1,\dots,a_n\in\{+1,-1\}$ whose aperiodic autocorrelations satisfy $\bigl|\sum_{i=1}^{n-k}a_ia_{i+k}\bigr|\le1$ for $1\le k<n$. Conjecture: no Barker sequence has length $n>13$. Odd lengths were settled by Turyn and Storer (1961); an even-length one with $n>4$ would give a circulant Hadamard matrix of order $n$, so the open case is even $n>4$.

wpu-016.statement: For each $n\ge1$ determine $D(n)=\max\{|\det M| : M\in\{-1,1\}^{n\times n}\}$ (equivalently, $D(n)/2^{n-1}$ is the largest determinant of an $(n-1)\times(n-1)$ matrix with entries in $\{0,1\}$). Hadamard's inequality gives $D(n)\le n^{n/2}$, with equality exactly when a Hadamard matrix of order $n$ exists; the exact value is unknown for infinitely many $n$.

wpu-021.statement: Collection of conjectures of I. Kaplansky. Group rings: for a field $K$ and torsion-free group $G$, (i) $K[G]$ has no zero divisors; (ii) its only idempotents are $0$ and $1$; (iii) every unit is trivial, $u=\lambda g$ with $\lambda\in K^\times$, $g\in G$. Also: every homomorphism from $C(X)$ ($X$ compact Hausdorff) to a Banach algebra is continuous; finite $u$-invariants of fields are powers of $2$; and ten conjectures on Hopf algebras.

statement_sources.label: Gardam, A counterexample to the unit conjecture for group rings, Ann. of Math. 194 (2021) (arXiv 2102.11818)
Formal Conjectures: Kaplansky.lean

wpu-022.statement: Köthe (1930): in every associative ring $R$, is the sum of two nil left ideals again a nil left ideal? By Krempa and Amitsur this is equivalent to: for every nil two-sided ideal $I\subseteq R$ the matrix ideal $M_2(I)\subseteq M_2(R)$ is nil; and to: $N[x]$ is Jacobson radical for every nil ring $N$.

wpu-025.name: Pierce–Birkhoff conjecture
wpu-025.review_reason: Recent (Sep 2026) AI-assisted counterexample with Lean proofs; no expert response found yet. Could move to solved quickly if accepted; check the Lean statement matches the semialgebraic-partition formulation.
wpu-025.statement: Let $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ be continuous and piecewise polynomial: there are finitely many polynomials $g_1,\dots,g_r\in\mathbb{R}[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and a finite semialgebraic partition of $\mathbb{R}^n$ such that $f$ agrees with some $g_i$ on each piece. Pierce and Birkhoff (as formulated by Henriksen–Isbell, 1962) conjectured that every such $f$ equals $\max_i\min_j f_{ij}$ for finitely many polynomials $f_{ij}$. It is known for $n\le2$ (Mahé).

statement_sources.label: Lai–Lim–Ren, Pierce–Birkhoff conjecture is false (arXiv 2609.10420v1), Conjecture 1

wpu-026.statement: Let $M$ be a matroid of rank $n$ and $B_1,\dots,B_n$ bases of $M$ (taken as disjoint copies, so repeated elements are allowed). Rota (1989) conjectured that the $n^2$ elements can be placed in an $n\times n$ array whose $i$-th row lists the elements of $B_i$ and each of whose columns is a basis of $M$; equivalently, $B_1\cup\dots\cup B_n$ splits into $n$ disjoint transversal bases.

wpu-028.name: Serre's positivity conjecture
wpu-028.statement: Let $R$ be a regular local ring and $M,N$ nonzero finitely generated $R$-modules with $M\otimes_RN$ of finite length and $\dim M+\dim N=\dim R$. Serre conjectured $\chi(M,N)=\sum_{i\ge0}(-1)^i\,\ell_R\bigl(\mathrm{Tor}^R_i(M,N)\bigr)>0$. It suffices to treat $M=R/P$, $N=R/Q$ with $P,Q$ prime ideals. Serre proved it when $R$ is equicharacteristic or unramified; the ramified mixed-characteristic case is open.

wpu-033.name: Andrews–Curtis conjecture
wpu-033.statement: Let $\langle x_1,\dots,x_n\mid r_1,\dots,r_n\rangle$ be a balanced presentation of the trivial group. Can it always be transformed into $\langle x_1,\dots,x_n\mid x_1,\dots,x_n\rangle$ by finitely many moves that replace some $r_i$ by $r_i^{-1}$, by $r_ir_j$ with $j\ne i$, or by a conjugate $wr_iw^{-1}$ ($w$ in the free group)? (The stable version also permits adding or deleting a generator $x_{n+1}$ together with the relator $x_{n+1}$.)

wpu-035.name: Guralnick–Thompson conjecture
wpu-035.statement: Fix $g\ge0$. Call a transitive permutation group $G\le S_n$ a genus-$g$ group if it is generated by some $x_1,\dots,x_r$ with $x_1\cdots x_r=1$ and $\sum_i(n-\#\{\text{orbits of }\langle x_i\rangle\})=2(n+g-1)$, i.e. $G$ is the monodromy group of a degree-$n$ branched cover of $\mathbb P^1$ by a connected curve of genus $g$. Guralnick–Thompson (1990): for each $g$, only finitely many nonabelian simple groups other than alternating groups occur as composition factors of genus-$g$ groups.

statement_sources.label: Aschbacher, On conjectures of Guralnick and Thompson, J. Algebra 135 (1990)
Frohardt–Magaard, Annals of Math. 154 (2001)

wpu-035.status_headline: Solved. Proved by Frohardt and Magaard (Annals of Math., 2001) after reductions by Aschbacher, Guralnick and Thompson.

Algebra 135 (1990). Solved S2 confirmed. Statement fix: the definition of genus-g group omitted transitivity; without it, adding fixed points (trivial genus-0 components) makes any monodromy group count as genus 0, so the conjecture as written would be false. Rewritten with transitive groups and connected curves.

wpu-040.statement: Norton (1987): to each element $g$ of the Monster $\mathbb M$ one can attach a graded projective representation $V(g)$ of $C_{\mathbb M}(g)$, compatibly with conjugation, so that for commuting $g,h$ the graded trace $Z(g,h;\tau)$ of a lift of $h$ on $V(g)$ is constant or a genus-zero Hauptmodul, $Z(g,h;\gamma\tau)$ is proportional to $Z(g^ah^c,g^bh^d;\tau)$ for $\gamma\in\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$, and $Z(g,h)$ is a multiple of $J$ only when $g=h=1$.

This transfers his Schubert-variety results to all characteristics and to $\mathbb Z$.

wpu-047.name: Kazhdan–Lusztig conjectures
wpu-047.statement: Let $\mathfrak g$ be a complex semisimple Lie algebra with Weyl group $W$; for $w\in W$ let $M_w$ be the Verma module of highest weight $-w\rho-\rho$ and $L_w$ its simple quotient. Kazhdan and Lusztig (1979) conjectured $\mathrm{ch}\,L_w=\sum_{y\le w}(-1)^{\ell(w)-\ell(y)}P_{y,w}(1)\,\mathrm{ch}\,M_y$, where $P_{y,w}$ are the Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials; equivalently, Verma multiplicities in category $\mathcal O$ are values $P_{w_0w,w_0y}(1)$.

statement_sources.label: Kazhdan–Lusztig, Representations of Coxeter groups and Hecke algebras, Invent. Math. 53 (1979)

wpu-049.name: Brennan conjecture
wpu-049.statement: Let $\Omega\subsetneq\mathbb{C}$ be a simply connected domain and $\varphi:\Omega\to\mathbb{D}$ a conformal bijection onto the unit disk. Brennan conjectured that $\int_\Omega |\varphi'(z)|^p\,dA(z)<\infty$ for every $p$ with $4/3<p<4$; the Koebe function shows the range cannot be enlarged. Integrability is known for $4/3<p<p_0$ with some $p_0$ only slightly above $3$, so the conjecture concerns the remaining exponents below $4$.

wpu-050.statement: Fuglede's spectral set conjecture: a measurable set $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ with $0<|\Omega|<\infty$ admits an orthogonal basis of exponentials $\{e^{2\pi i\lambda\cdot x}\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ for $L^2(\Omega)$ if and only if $\Omega$ tiles $\mathbb{R}^d$ by translations. Both directions are known to fail for $d\ge3$, and the conjecture holds for convex bodies in all dimensions. The question here: does it hold for general (nonconvex) sets (a) in dimension $d=1$, and (b) in dimension $d=2$?

wpu-051.name: Goodman's conjecture

partial_results.text: Treats p-valent functions of the form P(phi) with P a polynomial and phi univalent, reducing the conjecture there to coefficient inequalities for univalent functions.
partial_results.title: Goodman's Conjecture and the Coefficients of Univalent Functions (Lyzzaik–Styer, Proc. AMS 1978)

wpu-051.statement: Let $f(z)=\sum_{n\ge1}b_nz^n$ be analytic and at most $p$-valent in the unit disk. Goodman (1948) conjectured that for all $n>p$ one has $|b_n|\le\sum_{k=1}^{p}C_{p,k,n}|b_k|$, where $C_{p,k,n}=\dfrac{2k\,(n+p)!}{(p-k)!\,(p+k)!\,(n-p-1)!\,(n^2-k^2)}$. For $p=1$ this reduces to the Bieberbach bound $|b_n|\le n|b_1|$.

statement_sources.label: A. W. Goodman, On some determinants related to p-valent functions, Trans. AMS (1948)

wpu-054.statement: For $P(x)=a\prod_{i}(x-\alpha_i)\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ let $M(P)=|a|\prod_i\max(1,|\alpha_i|)$ be its Mahler measure. Lehmer's problem: is there an absolute constant $c>1$ such that every $P\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ with $M(P)>1$ (equivalently, not a product of $\pm x^k$ and cyclotomic polynomials) satisfies $M(P)\ge c$? Lehmer's degree-10 polynomial gives $M\approx1.17628$, conjectured to be the minimum.

statement_sources.label: C. Smyth, The Mahler measure of algebraic numbers: a survey (arXiv math/0701397)

wpu-056.name: Pompeiu problem
wpu-056.review_reason: Solved rests on S2 'independent re-proof' plus a maintainer-reviewed formal statement; all papers are unrefereed (Aug-Oct 2026). wpu-056.statement: A bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n\ge2$) has the Pompeiu property if the only continuous $f$ with $\int_{\sigma(\Omega)}f=0$ for every rigid motion $\sigma$ is $f\equiv0$. Pompeiu's conjecture: a bounded simply connected domain with Lipschitz boundary (connected complement of its closure) fails the Pompeiu property only if it is a ball. Equivalently (Williams), the overdetermined Neumann problem $\Delta u+\lambda u=0$, $u=1$, $\partial_\nu u=0$ on $\partial\Omega$ has nonconstant solutions only on balls (Schiffer).

wpu-062.name: Are there infinitely many Lehmer pairs?
wpu-062.statement: Let $\gamma_-<\gamma_+$ be consecutive simple positive zeros of Riemann's $\Xi(t)$, $\Delta=\gamma_+-\gamma_-$, and $g=\sum_{\gamma\ne\gamma_\pm}\big[(\gamma-\gamma_-)^{-2}+(\gamma-\gamma_+)^{-2}\big]$ over the other zeros. Csordas, Smith and Varga call $\{\gamma_-,\gamma_+\}$ a Lehmer pair if $\Delta^2 g<4/5$. Are there infinitely many Lehmer pairs?

wpu-064.statement: Let $K_n$ be the set of $n\times n$ real matrices with nonnegative entries summing to $n$. For $A\in K_n$ with row sums $r_i$ and column sums $c_j$, set $\phi(A)=\prod_{i}r_i+\prod_{j}c_j-\operatorname{per}(A)$. Dittert's conjecture: for every $n$, the maximum of $\phi$ on $K_n$ is attained only at the uniform matrix $J_n/n$, where it equals $2-n!/n^n$.

wpu-069.name: No-three-in-line problem
wpu-069.statement: Let $f(n)$ be the largest number of points of the $n\times n$ grid $\{0,\dots,n-1\}^2$ such that no three lie on a common line (of any slope). Since each row holds at most two points, $f(n)\le 2n$. Is $f(n)=2n$ for all large $n$? Guy and Kelly conjectured that it is not; their probabilistic heuristic, in its later corrected form, predicts $f(n)\sim(\pi/\sqrt3)\,n$.

wpu-070.name: Rudin's conjecture
wpu-070.statement: Let $Q(N)$ be the maximum, over non-constant arithmetic progressions $a, a+q, \dots, a+(N-1)q$ of positive integers, of the number of perfect squares among the $N$ terms. Rudin conjectured $Q(N)=O(\sqrt N)$. The strong form asserts that for every $N\ge6$ the maximum is attained by the progression $24n+1$, i.e. $Q(N)=Q(N;24,1)$.

If only the Q case counts, it is a special case and the entry should be open. The Arnold–Givental proof (Bai–Shelukhin–Wang–Xu, Aug 2026) is an unrefereed preprint. OpenAI family 347 (quadric threefold example Lean-checked) and Jiao (ChatGPT-assisted, S^2×S^2) claim counterexamples to the strong critical-number form; both unreviewed.
wpu-079.statement: Arnold conjecture: on a closed symplectic manifold $(M,\omega)$, a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism $\varphi$ has at least as many fixed points as a smooth function on $M$ must have critical points (Morse number if $\varphi$ is nondegenerate); the homological form asks $\#\mathrm{Fix}(\varphi)\ge\sum_i\dim H_i(M;\mathbb F)$. Arnold–Givental: if $L=\mathrm{Fix}(\tau)$ for an anti-symplectic involution $\tau$ and $\varphi(L)\pitchfork L$, then $\#(\varphi(L)\cap L)\ge\dim H_*(L;\mathbb F_2)$.

statement_sources.label: Bai–Shelukhin–Wang–Xu, arXiv:2608.27242 (statement of the Arnold–Givental conjecture)
Fukaya–Ono, Arnold conjecture and Gromov–Witten invariant, Topology 38 (1999)

wpu-092.statement: (Rudnick–Sarnak) Let $M$ be a compact Riemannian manifold of negative sectional curvature and $(\phi_j)$ any sequence of $L^2$-normalized Laplace eigenfunctions with eigenvalues $\lambda_j\to\infty$. Must the microlocal lifts of $|\phi_j|^2$ converge weak-* to the Liouville measure on $S^*M$, i.e. is Liouville the only quantum limit, with no exceptional subsequence? (In particular $|\phi_j|^2\,d\mathrm{vol}$ would tend to normalized volume.)

statement_sources.label: Rudnick–Sarnak, The behaviour of eigenstates of arithmetic hyperbolic manifolds, Comm. Math. Phys. 161 (1994)

Statement fix: the old text called convergence of |phi_j|^2 dvol 'equivalent' to Liouville being the only quantum limit on S*M. Only the latter (phase-space) statement is QUE, and the base-space one is weaker. It should also cover every sequence of eigenfunctions, not one chosen basis. Rewritten.

wpu-104.category_rationale: The threshold dimension is known only for very small n (e.g. 3^3 and 4^3 are first-player wins). No general determination exists.

evidence.claimant: S. W. Golomb, A. W. Hales
evidence.note: Discusses win/draw regions in n–k space and conjectures a critical n for each dimension. Small cases only.
evidence.title: Hypercube Tic-Tac-Toe
evidence.venue: More Games of No Chance, MSRI Publications 42

wpu-104.name: Smallest dimension for a first-player win in n^d tic-tac-toe
wpu-104.statement: In the $n^d$ game, players alternately claim cells of the cube $\{1,\dots,n\}^d$, and the first to own all $n$ cells of some geometric line (including diagonals) wins. By the Hales–Jewett theorem, for each $n$ the first player has a winning strategy once $d$ is large enough. For each $n$, determine the least such $d$.

statement_sources.label: Golomb and Hales, Hypercube Tic-Tac-Toe, in More Games of No Chance (MSRI Publ. 42, 2002)

wpu-104.status_headline: Open. Thresholds are known only for tiny boards (e.g. n = 3: 3^2 draw, 3^3 first-player win; 4^3 is a first-player win). The general dependence on n is unknown.
wpu-104.verifier_checks: Opened the Golomb–Hales PDF (MSRI Publ. 42, 2002): the problem is framed as critical n for given k, equivalent to the list's question. The statement shares at most 7 words with the Hales–Jewett article. Open confirmed.

wpu-106.category_rationale: Chess is far from solved. Exhaustive tablebases cover only positions with few pieces.
wpu-106.name: Outcome of perfectly played chess
wpu-106.statement: Under the standard rules of chess, with draw rules that make every game finite (e.g. automatic draws by fivefold repetition or 75 moves without capture or pawn move), what is the game-theoretic value of the initial position: a forced win for White, a forced win for Black, or a draw?

statement_sources.label: Shannon, Programming a computer for playing chess (Philosophical Magazine, 1950)

wpu-106.status_headline: Open. Endgame tablebases solve every position with at most 7 pieces, but the value of the starting position is unknown. It is widely believed to be a draw.
wpu-106.verifier_checks: Statement checked (well-defined via automatic draw rules). No sources needed for open; statement_sources is empty, which is acceptable but could be filled. Open.

wpu-108.category_rationale: Only small boards have been solved. Komi on 19×19 is set empirically.

evidence.note: Computer search shows 5×5 Go is a first-player win by 25 points (whole board), with the first move in the centre.
evidence.title: 5x5 Go is solved

wpu-108.name: Perfect komi in Go
wpu-108.statement: On the standard $19\times19$ Go board under a fixed rule set (e.g. area scoring with a specified superko rule), determine the margin by which Black wins or loses from the empty board with perfect play by both sides. This 'perfect komi' is the compensation to White that would make the game a draw.

statement_sources.label: van der Werf, 5x5 Go is solved (2002 announcement)

wpu-108.status_headline: Open for 19×19. Small boards are solved (5×5: Black wins by 25 points, van der Werf 2002). Tournament komi (6.5–7.5) is set empirically, not proved.
wpu-108.verifier_checks: Opened van der Werf's 5x5 announcement (20 Oct 2002; first-player win by 25 points). Open confirmed.

wpu-110.category_rationale: Neither the exact values nor the growth constant are known. AI-found constructions (FunSearch, X-evolve) only improve lower bounds, hence ai-partial.

evidence.note: Upper bound r_3(n) = O(2.756^n) via the Croot–Lev–Pach polynomial method.
evidence.title: On large subsets of F_q^n with no three-term arithmetic progression

evidence.note: LLM-guided program search found larger cap sets and admissible sets, raising the asymptotic lower bound to about 2.2202^n.
evidence.title: Mathematical discoveries from program search with large language models

evidence.note: Claims a larger admissible set giving cap set constant ≥ 2.2203.
evidence.title: X-evolve: Solution space evolution powered by large language models

wpu-110.name: Largest cap set in F_3^n

partial_results.text: r_3(n) ≤ O(2.756^n) (Ellenberg–Gijswijt).
partial_results.title: Polynomial-method upper bound

partial_results.text: AI-discovered admissible sets give r_3(n) ≥ 2.2202^n for large n.
partial_results.title: FunSearch lower bound

wpu-110.statement: A cap set in $\mathbb F_3^n$ is a set with no three distinct points on a line, equivalently no nontrivial solution of $x+y+z=0$. Let $r_3(n)$ be its maximum size. Determine $r_3(n)$ for every $n$ (exact values are known only for $n\le6$) and the growth constant $\lim_n r_3(n)^{1/n}$, known to lie between about $2.22$ and $2.756$.

statement_sources.label: Ellenberg and Gijswijt, On large subsets of F_q^n with no three-term arithmetic progression (arXiv:1605.09223)
Tyrrell, New Lower Bounds for Cap Sets (arXiv:2209.10045)

wpu-110.status_headline: Open. The growth constant lies between ≈2.2202 (FunSearch, Nature 2023; ≈2.2203 in later preprints) and 2.756 (Ellenberg–Gijswijt 2017). Exact values are known for n ≤ 6.
wpu-110.verifier_checks: Opened the Nature FunSearch page (Nature 625, 468; text: cap set capacity lower bound 2.2202), arXiv 2508.07932 (X-evolve, C ≥ 2.2203), 1605.09223 and 2209.10045. An arXiv search (cap set) found no 2026 bound change beyond structural results (2606.12194, 2604.26989). Open + ai-partial is correct. Statement accurate (exact values n ≤ 6).

wpu-111.category_rationale: Periodicity is proven game by game by computation. Several short octal games remain unresolved, and no general argument exists.
wpu-111.name: Periodicity of finite octal games
wpu-111.statement: An octal game is an impartial take-and-break game encoded by an octal code $d_0.d_1d_2\dots$, where digit $d_i$ says in how many heaps (0, 1 or 2) a heap may be left after removing $i$ tokens. The game is finite if only finitely many $d_i$ are nonzero. Guy's conjecture: is the Sprague–Grundy sequence $G(0),G(1),G(2),\dots$ of every finite octal game eventually periodic?

statement_sources.label: Flammenkamp, Sprague-Grundy Values of Octal-Games (computational tables)

wpu-111.status_headline: Open. Many individual octal games are proved periodic by computation (Guy–Smith periodicity test), but several remain unresolved after extensive computation.
wpu-111.verifier_checks: Flammenkamp octal page resolves. An arXiv search (octal games) found only partizan/misère work (2608.13273). Guy's conjecture is open; statement correct.

wpu-112.category_rationale: Periodicity is neither proved nor refuted. Computations of billions of values show no period yet.

evidence.note: Computational record of G(n) (page last updated 2021-04-10). Hoey computed all values up to 1.1×10^10 (1995–96); later runs reach about 2^38. No periodicity seen; the rare 'sparse' values would have to die out.
evidence.title: Sprague-Grundy Values of Grundy's Game

wpu-112.name: Periodicity of Grundy's game
wpu-112.statement: In Grundy's game, a move splits one heap into two nonempty heaps of different sizes, and a player who cannot move loses. Is the sequence $G(n)$ of Sprague–Grundy values of a single heap of $n$ tokens eventually periodic (as Berlekamp, Conway and Guy conjectured)?

statement_sources.label: Flammenkamp, Sprague-Grundy Values of Grundy's Game (computational record)

wpu-112.status_headline: Open. Values computed well beyond 10^10 heap sizes (Hoey; Flammenkamp) show no periodicity. The conjecture remains unresolved.
wpu-112.verifier_checks: Opened Flammenkamp's Grundy page: Hoey computed up to 11×10^9 (1995–96), statistics go up to 2^38 + 150·2^26, and the page was last updated 2021-04-10. The evidence date (2000-12) and note are refreshed. An arXiv search found no periodicity proof. The statement is accurate.

wpu-113.category_rationale: Optimal symmetric strategies are known only for n = 2, 3. Anderson–Weber is suboptimal for n = 4 (Weber 2009) and, per a 2026 preprint, for every n ≥ 4. The optimum for n ≥ 4 is unknown.

evidence.note: Exhibits a strategy slightly better than Anderson–Weber for n = 4. Recalls that Anderson–Weber is optimal for n = 2 and n = 3.
evidence.title: The Anderson-Weber strategy is not optimal for symmetric rendezvous search on K4

evidence.claimant: J. Cembrano, F. Fischer, M. Klimm
evidence.note: Explicit symmetric strategy that beats Anderson–Weber for every finite n ≥ 4. The authors state that optimal strategies for n ≥ 4 remain open.
evidence.title: Faster Symmetric Rendezvous on Four or More Locations

wpu-113.name: Rendezvous problem
wpu-113.review_reason: The list gives only 'Rendezvous problem'. I chose the symmetric rendezvous problem on K_n (Mozart café), which the linked article highlights. Other variants (e.g. on the line) are also open.
wpu-113.statement: Symmetric rendezvous search on $n$ locations (complete graph $K_n$): two players start at distinct, indistinguishable locations, cannot agree on labels in advance, and must use the same randomised strategy. Each period each player stays or moves to any location. Find the strategy minimising the expected meeting time. Anderson–Weber's strategy is optimal for $n=2,3$. What is optimal for $n\ge4$?

statement_sources.label: Weber, The Anderson-Weber strategy is not optimal for symmetric rendezvous search on K4 (arXiv:0912.0670)
Alpern, The rendezvous search problem, SIAM J. Control Optim. 33 (1995)

wpu-113.status_headline: Open. The optimal symmetric strategy is known only for n = 2, 3. Anderson–Weber is beaten for n = 4 (Weber 2009 note) and every n ≥ 4 (2026 preprint); the optimum is unknown.
wpu-113.verifier_checks: Opened arXiv 0912.0670 (Weber, K4, unpublished note). An arXiv API search found 2604.02058v2 (Cembrano–Fischer–Klimm, 2026), which beats Anderson–Weber for all n ≥ 4, calls Weber 2009 an unpublished manuscript, and says optimal strategies for n ≥ 4 remain open (PDF read). It is added to evidence and the headline is updated. The Alpern DOI returns 403 to bots and was not verified. Category open is correct.

If $K_X$ (resp. $K_X+\Delta$) is nef, is it semiample, i.e. is some positive multiple $mK_X$ base-point free?

wpu-115.category_rationale: Known in dimension ≤ 1 (Quillen); no general resolution found. Not to be confused with the Bass trace conjecture for group rings.
wpu-115.name: Bass conjecture (finite generation of K-groups)
wpu-115.statement: Let $A$ be a commutative regular ring of finite type over $\mathbb{Z}$. Is the Quillen K-group $K_n(A)$ finitely generated for every $n\ge 0$? (A closely related form asks the same for the G-theory groups $G_n(X)$ of every scheme $X$ of finite type over $\mathbb{Z}$.)

wpu-115.status_headline: Open. Known for rings and schemes of dimension at most one (Quillen); no recent resolution found.

Statement called the G-theory form 'equivalent', which is not established in general (it relies on resolution-type arguments); reworded as a related form.

wpu-116.category_rationale: Known when A contains a field (Lindel, Popescu) and in low dimension; the mixed-characteristic case remains open. Recent work treats torsor generalizations only.
wpu-116.name: Bass–Quillen conjecture
wpu-116.statement: Let $A$ be a regular Noetherian ring and $n\ge1$. Is every finitely generated projective module $P$ over $A[t_1,\dots,t_n]$ extended from $A$, i.e. $P\cong Q\otimes_A A[t_1,\dots,t_n]$ for some finitely generated projective $A$-module $Q$?

statement_sources.label: The Bass–Quillen conjecture for torsors over valuation rings (arXiv 2503.10163)
On the generalized Bass–Quillen conjecture in dimension 2 (arXiv 2512.18868)

wpu-116.status_headline: Open in general (notably mixed characteristic). Known for regular rings containing a field; 2025 work extends torsor variants.

wpu-120.statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $0$, $S=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, and $f_1,\dots,f_r$ general forms of degrees $d_1,\dots,d_r$. statement_sources.label: Wang–Zhang, Fröberg's Conjecture for Quintics and Septics in Four Variables (arXiv 2608.24797)

wpu-123.name: Hartshorne's conjectures on subvarieties with ample normal bundle
wpu-123.review_reason: Bullet has no linked article; identified via its BPS 1990 reference. Could be confused with Hartshorne's complete-intersection conjecture (open). Partial relies on FL counterexample to A, reported by Ottem rather than linked directly.
wpu-123.statement: Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety. (A) If $Y\subset X$ is a smooth subvariety with ample normal bundle, does some multiple of the cycle $Y$ move in a family covering $X$? (B) If $Y,Z\subset X$ are smooth subvarieties with ample normal bundles and $\dim Y+\dim Z\ge\dim X$, must $Y\cap Z\neq\emptyset$?

statement_sources.label: Ottem, On subvarieties with ample normal bundle (arXiv 1309.2263)
Peternell, Submanifolds with ample normal bundles and a conjecture of Hartshorne (arXiv 0804.1023)

wpu-123.status_headline: Partial. Conjecture A (multiples move) is false in general by a Fulton–Lazarsfeld counterexample; Conjecture B (intersection) is open, known in many special cases.
wpu-123.verifier_checks: Opened arXiv 1309.2263v2 (Ottem): states Hartshorne's Conjectures A (some multiple moves in a covering family) and B (intersection), and records that Fulton–Lazarsfeld showed A false when dim Y ≥ 2 (curve case open). Crossref: Ottem published in JEMS 18 (2016). Opened arXiv 0804.1023v1 (Peternell: B 'wide open', cites BPS90). Crossref confirms BPS 1990 Math. Ann. title. Two named conjectures under one heading, A answered negatively in refereed work, B open, so partial P2 is defensible. Updated Ottem item to refereed/JEMS.

wpu-124.category_rationale: No accepted resolution found; the Euclidean analogue (Dehn–Sydler) is settled but the spherical and hyperbolic cases remain open (tied to rigidity conjectures on K_3 of C).
wpu-124.name: Scissors congruence in spherical and hyperbolic 3-space (generalized Hilbert third problem)
wpu-124.statement: Let $X$ be the round 3-sphere $S^3$ or hyperbolic 3-space $\mathbb{H}^3$. If two compact polyhedra in $X$ have equal volume and equal Dehn invariant $\sum_e \ell(e)\otimes\theta(e)$ (edge length tensored with dihedral angle), must they be scissors-congruent, i.e. cut into finitely many pieces that are pairwise congruent under isometries of $X$? (Question of Dupont and Sah; the Euclidean analogue holds by Sydler's theorem.)

statement_sources.label: Campbell–Zakharevich, Hilbert's third problem and a conjecture of Goncharov (arXiv 1910.07112v8)
Calegari, Notes on scissors congruence (U. Chicago course notes)

wpu-124.status_headline: Open. Solved in Euclidean 3-space (Sydler 1965); the spherical and hyperbolic analogues remain open. No 2025–2026 resolution found.
wpu-124.verifier_checks: Opened arXiv 1910.07112 v6 and v8: the paper is Campbell–Zakharevich, 'Hilbert's third problem and a conjecture of Goncharov' (the label given was wrong; v5 was a withdrawal), whose intro states the Dupont–Sah question; opened Calegari notes (course notes, do not state the S^3/H^3 question explicitly). Dupont's .ps link is dead. arXiv search (scissors congruence, 2025-2026) found no resolution. Statement narrowed to dimension 3 (the higher-dimensional parenthetical used an undefined Dehn invariant).

wpu-140.name: Erdős–Oler conjecture
wpu-140.statement: Let $s(n)$ be the side length of the smallest equilateral triangle that contains $n$ non-overlapping unit disks. wpu-151.statement: Let $M^n$ ($n\ge2$) be a Cartan–Hadamard manifold, i.e. complete, simply connected, with sectional curvature $\le 0$. The generalized form uses a curvature bound $\kappa\le0$ and balls in the model space of curvature $\kappa$.

wpu-165.name: Kobon triangle problem
wpu-165.statement: For $k\ge3$ let $K(k)$ be the maximum number of pairwise non-overlapping triangles whose sides lie on the lines of an arrangement of $k$ lines in the Euclidean plane (each triangle being a face of the arrangement). Determine $K(k)$ for every $k$. Tamura's bound $K(k)\le\lfloor k(k-2)/3\rfloor$ and refinements of it are attained for some $k$, but the exact value is unknown for many $k$.

statement_sources.label: Savchuk, Constructing Optimal Kobon Triangle Arrangements via Table Encoding, SAT Solving, and Heuristic Straightening (arXiv 2025, v2 2026)

wpu-167.name: McMullen problem (projective transformations into convex position)
wpu-167.statement:
Let $
u(d)$ be the largest integer $N$ such that every set of $N$ points in general position in $\mathbb{R}^d$ can be mapped by some admissible projective transformation onto the vertex set of a convex polytope. Determine $
u(d)$; it is conjectured that $
u(d)=2d+1$, which holds for $d\le4$, while in general only $2d+1\le
u(d)\le2d+\lceil (d+1)/2ceil$ is known.

statement_sources.label: Garcia-Colin & Larman, Projective Equivalences of k-neighbourly Polytopes (arXiv 2013)
Hernández-Ortiz, Knauer & Montejano, On k-neighborly reorientations of oriented matroids (arXiv 2023)

wpu-168.name: Opaque forest problem (shortest opaque sets)
wpu-168.statement: An opaque set for a planar convex region $K$ is a set meeting every line that intersects $K$. Determine the minimum total length of an opaque set (or opaque forest of segments) for basic shapes — notably the unit square (conjectured $\sqrt2+\sqrt6/2\approx2.639$), the equilateral triangle and the unit disk — and decide whether a shortest opaque set always exists and, for polygons, can be taken to be a finite forest.

Kawamura, Moriyama, Otachi & Pach, A lower bound on opaque sets (arXiv 2014)

wpu-169.statement: Let $t_3(n)$ be the maximum number of lines containing exactly three points of a set of $n$ points in the real plane. Determine $t_3(n)$ for every $n$. wpu-170.statement: Let $u(n)$ be the maximum number of unordered pairs at Euclidean distance exactly $1$ among $n$ points of $\mathbb{R}^2$. Determine the asymptotic growth of $u(n)$. Classically $u(n)=O(n^{4/3})$; Erdős conjectured $u(n)\le n^{1+O(1/\log\log n)}$, but in 2026 it was shown that $u(n)\ge n^{1.014}$ for infinitely many $n$, so the correct exponent (if any) lies in $[1.014,4/3]$.

wpu-171.name: k-sets and halving lines: matching upper and lower bounds
wpu-171.statement: For a set $P$ of $n$ points in general position in the plane, a $k$-set is a $k$-element subset that can be cut off from the rest by a line; let $e_k(n)$ be the maximum number of $k$-sets over all such $P$, and $h(n)=e_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}(n)$ the maximum number of halving lines. Determine the order of $e_k(n)$; the known bounds $n\,e^{\Omega(\sqrt{\log k})}\le e_k(n)\le O(nk^{1/3})$ (in particular $h(n)$ between $n e^{\Omega(\sqrt{\log n})}$ and $O(n^{4/3})$) are far apart.

statement_sources.label: Kovács & Tóth, Dense point sets with many halving lines (arXiv 2017)

wpu-172.name: Do crossing-minimal point sets maximize halving lines?
wpu-172.statement: For a set $P$ of $n$ points in general position in the plane let $\overline{cr}(P)$ be the number of crossing pairs of segments in the straight-line drawing of $K_n$ on $P$ and $h(P)$ its number of halving lines. Is it true that for every $n$, every $P$ attaining $\overline{cr}(P)=\overline{cr}(n)=\min_{|Q|=n}\overline{cr}(Q)$ also attains $h(P)=h(n)=\max_{|Q|=n}h(Q)$? (The converse is known to fail.)

statement_sources.label: Aichholzer, García, Orden & Ramos, New lower bounds for the number of (≤k)-edges and the rectilinear crossing number of K_n (arXiv; DCG 2007)
Ábrego, Cetina, Fernández-Merchant, Leaños & Salazar, On (≤k)-edges, crossings, and halving lines of geometric drawings of K_n (arXiv 2011)

wpu-173.statement: Let $T(n)$ be the maximum number of pairwise disjoint tripods (unions of the three positive axis-parallel rays of unit cubes from a common apex cube) whose apexes lie in an $n\times n\times n$ grid; equivalently, the largest 2-comparable set of triples in $[n]^3$. Determine the order of growth of $T(n)$; the known bounds are $\Omega(n^{1.546})\le T(n)\le n^2/2^{\Omega(\log^* n)}$, and it is open whether $T(n)=n^{2-o(1)}$.

wpu-174.statement: For distinct points $x_1,\dots,x_n\in\mathbb{R}^3$, let $t_{ij}\in S^2\cong\mathbb{CP}^1$ be the direction of $x_j-x_i$ ($i\ne j$), and let $p_i$ be the binary form of degree $n-1$ with roots $\{t_{ij}:j\ne i\}$. Atiyah conjectured that $p_1,\dots,p_n$ are always linearly independent over $\mathbb{C}$, i.e. the $n\times n$ determinant of their coefficients never vanishes.

wpu-175.name: Bellman's lost-in-a-forest problem
wpu-175.statement: Given a planar region $F$ of known shape, find the least length of a path $\gamma$ such that a walker placed at an unknown point of $F$, facing an unknown direction, who traces $\gamma$ is guaranteed to hit $\partial F$. Equivalently, find the shortest curve no image of which under an orientation-preserving rigid motion lies in the interior of $F$. No general solution is known; exact optima are proved only for particular shapes.

statement_sources.label: Deng, A General Solution to Bellman's Lost-in-a-forest Problem, arXiv:2412.10686
Temerev & Doria, The exact solution of Bellman's lost-in-a-forest problem for the golden gnomon, arXiv:2607.24483

Equivalently, is there a triple of unknots, not all circles, that cannot be so arranged? Howards proposed the weaker conjecture for planar curves.

wpu-177.category_rationale: No resolution was found. Known results give bloomings for the source unfolding and for suitably refined nets only. wpu-177.name: Connelly's blooming conjecture

partial_results.text: The source unfolding of any convex polyhedron can be continuously bloomed, and any unfolding can be refined by linearly many extra cuts into one that blooms.
partial_results.title: Demaine et al. (2009/2011): source unfolding and refinements bloom

wpu-177.statement: A blooming of a net (a non-overlapping planar unfolding obtained by cutting the surface) of a convex polyhedron is a continuous motion from the folded polyhedron to the flat net in which each face stays rigid and no two faces ever intersect. Does every net of every convex polyhedron admit a blooming?

statement_sources.label: Demaine, Demaine, Hart, Iacono, Langerman, O'Rourke, Continuous Blooming of Convex Polyhedra, arXiv:0906.2461

wpu-177.status_headline: Open. Every convex polyhedron has some net that blooms (the source unfolding, or a refinement of any net), but whether every net blooms is unknown.
wpu-177.verifier_checks: Opened arXiv:0906.2461 and Crossref (Graphs and Combinatorics 27, 2011, so refereed, not just broadly accepted). Wikipedia 'Blooming (geometry)' (lead only) attaches Connelly's name to the some-net question, while the list asks whether every net blooms, which is open (Miller-Pak declined to conjecture). arXiv search found no new results. Category open stands; statement accurate, no copying.

wpu-178.category_rationale: Both named questions remain open, and no recent claims were found. Gowers' bounded-intersection variant was answered negatively, but it is not one of the two catalogued questions.

evidence.claimant: Omri Solan, Yaar Solomon, Barak Weiss
evidence.note: Resolves Gowers' variant: no set meets every unit-volume convex set in a number of points bounded above and below. Danzer's density question is untouched.
evidence.title: On problems of Danzer and Gowers and dynamics on the space of closed subsets of R^d

wpu-178.name: Danzer's problem and Conway's dead fly problem

partial_results.text: Shows substitution and cut-and-project point sets are not Danzer sets, and builds uniformly discrete dense forests via Ratner theory.
partial_results.title: Solomon–Weiss (2016): candidates ruled out; dense forests

wpu-178.statement: A Danzer set in $\mathbb{R}^d$ ($d\ge2$) is a set meeting every convex body of volume $1$. Danzer's problem: is there a Danzer set $Y$ of bounded density, i.e. $\#(Y\cap B(0,T))=O(T^d)$? Conway's dead fly problem (stronger): is there a Danzer set whose points are uniformly separated, $\inf_{y\ne y'\in Y}|y-y'|>0$?

statement_sources.label: Solomon & Weiss, Dense forests and Danzer sets (Ann. Sci. ENS 2016), arXiv:1406.3807
Solan, Solomon & Weiss, On problems of Danzer and Gowers, arXiv:1510.07179

wpu-178.status_headline: Open. Best constructions have growth O(T^d log T). Natural candidates (lattice unions, substitution and cut-and-project sets) are ruled out. Gowers' stronger variant is impossible.
wpu-178.verifier_checks: Opened arXiv:1406.3807v2 (Solomon-Weiss: substitution and cut-and-project sets not Danzer; O(T^d log T) construction) and arXiv:1510.07179v1 (Gowers' bounded-intersection variant impossible). arXiv search for Danzer density/separation: nothing new since 2021; not in openai/math. Statement precise (bounded density vs uniform separation); no copying.

wpu-179.category_rationale: Known for d ≤ 5 only (special cases), per the 2009 survey. No recent claims were found.
wpu-179.name: Hadwiger's conjecture on dissection into orthoschemes
wpu-179.statement: An orthoscheme (path-simplex) in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is a simplex whose vertices $v_0,\dots,v_d$ can be ordered so that the edges $v_{i-1}v_i$ are pairwise orthogonal. Hadwiger asked whether every $d$-simplex can be dissected into finitely many orthoschemes, and, in a stronger form, into at most $f(d)$ of them for some function $f$. Both forms are known only for $d\le5$.

statement_sources.label: Brandts, Korotov, Křížek, Šolc, On nonobtuse simplicial partitions, SIAM Review 51 (2009) (Conjecture 23)

wpu-179.status_headline: Open for d ≥ 6. Known in dimensions up to 5 (e.g. at most 12 orthoschemes for any tetrahedron, which is optimal).
wpu-179.verifier_checks: Opened Brandts-Korotov-Krizek-Solc SIAM Review 2009 PDF (Conjecture 23: every d-simplex dissects into finitely many path-simplices; proved only for d<=5; Lenhard 12 for tetrahedra, optimal by Bohm; 500 for d=4; 12,598,800 for d=5). Wikipedia article states the bounded f(d) form, which the statement also covers. arXiv search and openai/math: no new claims. No copying.

wpu-180.name: Ehrhart's volume conjecture

partial_results.text: Builds on Berman–Berndtsson to prove the sharp bound, with the equality characterization, for convex bodies contained in the polar of a lattice polytope.
partial_results.title: Nill & Paffenholz (2014): equality case for a class of bodies

wpu-180.review_reason: AI claim of the full inequality with a Lean proof against a Comparator statement. A Sept 2026 audit (Sienicki, arXiv) reports that a specialist review asks for major revision of this chapter. Check for later acceptance (would make it S2) or disputes. The equality refinement is claimed separately by an AI-generated preprint (Liu, Aug 2026).
wpu-180.statement: Let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex body whose barycenter is the origin and such that the origin is the only point of $\mathbb{Z}^n$ in the interior of $K$. Ehrhart conjectured that $\mathrm{vol}(K)\le (n+1)^n/n!$, the volume of the centered dilate $(n+1)\Delta_n-(1,\dots,1)$ of the standard simplex. (A further refinement asks that equality occur only for unimodular images of this simplex.)

statement_sources.label: Nill & Paffenholz, On the equality case in Ehrhart's volume conjecture (Adv. Geom. 2014), arXiv:1205.1270
OpenAI, Ten Advances in Mathematics and TCS, ch. 8 (states the inequality and its history)

wpu-182.name: Values of the Hermite constants

partial_results.text: The Leech lattice is the unique densest lattice in 24 dimensions, giving γ_24 = 4. The paper also gives a new proof for E8.
partial_results.title: Cohn–Kumar (2009): dimension 24

wpu-182.statement: For a lattice $L\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ of covolume 1, let $\lambda_1(L)$ be the length of a shortest nonzero vector. The Hermite constant is $\gamma_n=\max_L\lambda_1(L)^2$, equivalent to the densest lattice sphere packing in $\mathbb{R}^n$. Determine $\gamma_n$ for every $n$; it is classically known for $n\le8$, and for $n=24$ by Cohn–Kumar.

statement_sources.label: Cohn & Kumar, Optimality and uniqueness of the Leech lattice among lattices (Ann. of Math. 2009), arXiv:math/0403263
Dutour Sikirić & van Woerden, The lattice packing problem in dimension 9 by Voronoi's algorithm, arXiv:2508.20719

wpu-183.statement: A holyhedron is a polyhedron in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with finitely many planar faces, each a closed connected planar region with at least one polygonal hole, where hole boundaries are disjoint from one another and from the face's outer boundary. What is the smallest possible number of faces of a holyhedron?

statement_sources.label: D. Hatch, Holyhedron! (492-face example and Conway's prize)

wpu-183.status_headline: Open. Smallest known example improved from Hatch's 492 faces to 476 (2026, computer-verified with a Lean combinatorial certificate; unreviewed). The minimum is unknown.

wpu-194.statement: Let $P\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ be a polyhedron, not necessarily convex, whose boundary is a topological sphere, and suppose that translates of $P$ tile $\mathbb{R}^3$. Can the faces of $P$ always be grouped into connected patches so that the patches form a cell structure on $\partial P$? The structure should be combinatorially equivalent to the face lattice of one of Fedorov's five parallelohedra.

wpu-197.statement: For a knot type $K$, the ropelength $L(K)$ is the infimum, over closed curves $C$ of type $K$, of $\operatorname{length}(C)/D(C)$, where the thickness $D(C)$ is the largest diameter of an embedded normal tube around $C$ (twice its normal injectivity radius). Is there a general formula for $L(K)$, or even an exact value for a single nontrivial knot? None is known even for the trefoil: every nontrivial knot has $L(K)\ge15.66$, while numerically tightened trefoils reach about $16.37$.

statement_sources.label: Cantarella, Kusner & Sullivan, On the minimum ropelength of knots and links, Invent. Math. 150 (2002)

wpu-198.statement: Buck and Simon proved that there is a universal constant $a>0$ with $L(K)\ge a\,\mathrm{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$ for every knot $K$, where $L$ is ropelength and $\mathrm{Cr}$ is crossing number; the exponent $3/4$ cannot be improved in general, because some torus-type families have ropelength of order $\mathrm{Cr}^{3/4}$. wpu-201.name: Rupert property of convex polyhedra
wpu-201.statement: A convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ is Rupert if a congruent copy of $K$ can pass through a straight hole drilled through $K$: there are rigid motions $T_1,T_2$ with $\pi(T_1K)\subset\operatorname{int}\pi(T_2K)$, where $\pi$ is orthogonal projection to a plane. Does every convex polyhedron in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with nonempty interior have this property?

wpu-203.statement: Does there exist a polyhedron in $\mathbb{R}^3$ without self-intersections that has $f>7$ faces and in which every two faces share exactly one edge? The tetrahedron ($f=4$) and the Szilassi polyhedron ($f=7$) are the only known examples. If exactly three faces meet at each vertex, Euler's formula forces genus $(f-3)(f-4)/12$, so $f\equiv0,3,4,7\pmod{12}$ and the next candidate has $f=12$ and genus $6$.

wpu-209.statement: For a graph $G$ let $\gamma(G)$ be its domination number, $\gamma_\infty(G)$ the least size of a guard set that can answer every infinite attack sequence when, after each attack, one guard moves along an edge to the attacked vertex, and $\theta(G)$ the least number of cliques partitioning $V(G)$; always $\gamma\le\gamma_\infty\le\theta$. Does some graph satisfy $\gamma(G)=\gamma_\infty(G)<\theta(G)$? The $\gamma$–$\theta$ conjecture predicted that none does.

wpu-212.name: Monotonicity of the vertex colouring game
wpu-212.statement: In the vertex colouring game on a finite graph $G$ with $k$ colours, Alice and Bob alternately (Alice first) colour an uncoloured vertex with a colour different from those of its coloured neighbours; Alice wins if every vertex gets coloured. If Alice has a winning strategy with $k$ colours, must she also have one with $k+1$ colours?

statement_sources.label: Zhu, The game coloring number of planar graphs (JCTB 1999)

wpu-212.status_headline: Open. It is unknown whether Alice's winning with k colours implies winning with k+1 colours; even a weaker f(k) version is open.

wpu-213.statement: Let $n$ be even and $D\ge 2\lceil n/4\rceil-1$. Then every $D$-regular graph on $n$ vertices decomposes into perfect matchings, i.e. has chromatic index $D$. (Writing $n=2m$, the degree condition is $D\ge m$ for odd $m$ and $D\ge m-1$ for even $m$.)

Experts (Goedgebeur, Jooken, Máčajová, Mattiolo, Mazzuoccolo, et al.) verified these, built 52-vertex counterexamples with a purely theoretical proof and an infinite family. wpu-225.statement: (Chetwynd–Hilton, 1986.) Call $H\subseteq G$ $\Delta(G)$-overfull if $|E(H)|>\Delta(G)\lfloor |V(H)|/2\rfloor$. If $G$ is a simple graph on $n$ vertices with $\Delta(G)>n/3$, then $\chi'(G)=\Delta(G)+1$ (class 2) if and only if $G$ has a $\Delta(G)$-overfull subgraph $H$ with $\Delta(H)=\Delta(G)$.

wpu-233.statement: For all positive integers $m,n$, is $\mathrm{cr}(K_{m,n})$, the least number of edge crossings in a plane drawing of $K_{m,n}$, equal to $Z(m,n)=\lfloor m/2\rfloor\lfloor (m-1)/2\rfloor\lfloor n/2\rfloor\lfloor (n-1)/2\rfloor$? Zarankiewicz's drawings show $\mathrm{cr}(K_{m,n})\le Z(m,n)$; the question is whether some drawing of some $K_{m,n}$ uses fewer crossings.

wpu-241.statement: Call a graph geodetic if every two vertices are joined by a unique shortest path. A connected, non-complete strongly regular graph with parameters $(v,k,\lambda,\mu)$ is geodetic exactly when $\mu=1$. The only known examples are three Moore graphs: $C_5$, Petersen's graph and the Hoffman–Singleton graph (all with $\lambda=0$). Does an infinite family of such graphs exist, and does any example with $\lambda\ge 1$ (i.e., one that is not a Moore graph) exist?

wpu-247.name: Erdős–Hajnal conjecture

partial_results.text: Chudnovsky, Scott, Seymour and Spirkl proved the conjecture when H is the 5-cycle.
partial_results.title: Erdos-Hajnal for graphs with no 5-hole

partial_results.title: Induced subgraph density. I. A loglog step towards Erdos-Hajnal

wpu-247.statement: For every finite graph $H$ there is a constant $c=c(H)>0$ such that each $n$-vertex graph $G$ with no induced copy of $H$ has a homogeneous set of size at least $n^{c}$, that is, at least $n^{c}$ vertices that are pairwise adjacent or pairwise non-adjacent.

statement_sources.label: Chudnovsky, The Erdős–Hajnal conjecture—a survey, J. Graph Theory (2014)
Bucić, Nguyen, Scott, Seymour, Induced subgraph density I (arXiv)

wpu-247.status_headline: Open. Known for small or special forbidden graphs such as the 5-cycle. The best general bound is $2^{c\sqrt{\log n\log\log n}}$ (Bucić–Nguyen–Scott–Seymour).

wpu-248.category_rationale: No claimed resolution found. The planar (Tutte) and projective-planar (Thomas–Yu) analogues are theorems, but the torus case remains open.
wpu-248.name: Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture

partial_results.text: Thomas and Yu showed that every 5-connected graph embeddable in the torus has a Hamiltonian cycle.
partial_results.title: Five-connected toroidal graphs are Hamiltonian

partial_results.text: Thomas, Yu and Zang showed that every 4-connected toroidal graph has a Hamiltonian path.
partial_results.title: Hamilton paths in toroidal graphs

partial_results.text: Ellingham and Marshall show that natural generalizations of Thomassen's 4-connected toroidal graphs with an edge on no Hamiltonian cycle are critical. This explains why the planar inductive method does not carry over.
partial_results.title: Criticality of counterexamples to toroidal edge-Hamiltonicity

wpu-248.statement: Conjecture of Grünbaum and Nash-Williams: every 4-vertex-connected graph that embeds in the torus has a Hamiltonian cycle (the toroidal analogue of Tutte's theorem for 4-connected planar graphs).

statement_sources.label: Ellingham, Marshall, Criticality of counterexamples to toroidal edge-hamiltonicity (arXiv)

wpu-248.status_headline: Open. Planar (Tutte) and projective-planar (Thomas–Yu) analogues are theorems; for the torus, 5-connected graphs are Hamiltonian and 4-connected ones have Hamiltonian paths.

wpu-249.category_rationale: Only asymptotic bounds and special cases are known. A 2026 preprint shows the conjecture for infinite graphs of bounded degree is equivalent to the finite one.

wpu-249.name: Linear arboricity conjecture

partial_results.text: Lang and Postle show that for large Δ every graph of maximum degree Δ splits into at most Δ/2 + 3√Δ log⁴Δ linear forests, also in the list setting.
partial_results.title: An improved bound for the linear arboricity conjecture

wpu-249.statement: A linear forest is a graph whose components are paths. The linear arboricity conjecture (Akiyama–Exoo–Harary, 1980) asserts that the edges of every finite graph of maximum degree $\Delta$ can be partitioned into at most $\lceil(\Delta+1)/2\rceil$ linear forests.

statement_sources.label: Akiyama, Exoo, Harary, Covering and packing in graphs IV: Linear arboricity, Networks (1981)
Christoph et al., New bounds for linear arboricity and related problems (arXiv 2025)

wpu-249.status_headline: Open. Only asymptotic bounds: Δ/2 + 3√Δ log⁴Δ for large Δ (Lang–Postle) and Δ/2 + O(log n) (Christoph et al., 2025 preprint); small-Δ and large-girth cases are known.
wpu-249.verifier_checks: Spot-checked. arXiv API: Christoph et al. 2507.20500v1 confirmed (Delta/2+O(log n)). Aurichi-Monteiro-Rodrigues 2610.02065 (finite and infinite versions are equivalent) confirms the rationale. Mishra 2512.11240 covers large girth. So the headline's claim that Delta/2+O(log n) is 'the best general bound' was misleading: the two bounds are incomparable. Also partial_results listed an unaccepted preprint. wpu-250.category_rationale: No accepted full resolution. 2026 preprints prove long cycles of length $n^{2/3-o(1)}$ and then $n^{1-o(1)}$. A 2024 human claim covers only the odd-order case, which is a special case.

evidence.note: Every connected vertex-transitive graph on n vertices contains a cycle of length n^{1-o(1)}.
evidence.title: A nearly linear bound for the Lovász conjecture

evidence.note: Claims Hamiltonicity for odd-order connected vertex-transitive graphs (special case only); not accepted.
evidence.title: Proof of Lovász conjecture for odd order

wpu-250.name: Lovász conjecture
wpu-250.statement: Lovász (1969) asked whether every finite connected vertex-transitive graph has a Hamiltonian path; the conjecture is that it always does. A strengthened folklore form asks for a Hamiltonian cycle in all such graphs except $K_2$ and the four known exceptions (Petersen, Coxeter and their truncations).

statement_sources.label: Li, Methuku, A nearly linear bound for the Lovász conjecture (arXiv 2026)
Bucić, Christoph, Pokrovskiy, Steiner, Towards the Lovász conjecture via sublinear expanders (arXiv 2026)

wpu-250.status_headline: Open. 2026 preprints show every connected vertex-transitive graph on n vertices has a cycle of length n^{1−o(1)} (Li–Methuku), improving n^{2/3−o(1)}.
wpu-250.verifier_checks: Spot-checked (the entry includes a claim item). arXiv API confirms Li-Methuku 2609.38135v1 (2026-09-29; cycle length n^{1-o(1)}, improving n^{2/3-o(1)}). It confirms Bucic-Christoph-Pokrovskiy-Steiner 2606.09742v2 and Nakanishi 2407.00646v3, which claims Hamiltonicity only for odd order, a special case, so it is correctly a non-full human claim with no badge. A 'vertex-transitive AND hamiltonian' search finds no full claim (2608.02349 handles order 2pq only). The four known exceptions are stated correctly.

wpu-251.category_rationale: Glock et al. settled all sufficiently large orders, and many families and small orders are done. No complete answer covers every order, so the question as stated remains open in finitely many unresolved cases.

evidence.claimant: Stefan Glock, Felix Joos, Jaehoon Kim, Daniela Kühn, Deryk Osthus
evidence.note: Proves the required decomposition exists for every 2-factor when n is large enough. The threshold is not explicit.
evidence.title: Resolution of the Oberwolfach problem

wpu-251.name: Oberwolfach problem

partial_results.text: The Oberwolfach (and Hamilton–Waterloo) problem has a positive answer for all sufficiently large n.
partial_results.title: Resolution of the Oberwolfach problem

wpu-251.review_reason: The title 'Resolution of the Oberwolfach problem' covers only large n; small orders are not fully covered, so the entry is kept open. A reviewer may prefer a different reading.
wpu-251.statement: Ringel's Oberwolfach problem: for odd $n$ and a 2-regular graph $F$ on $n$ vertices, decide whether $K_n$ decomposes into $(n-1)/2$ edge-disjoint copies of $F$ (for even $n$, $K_n$ minus a perfect matching into $(n-2)/2$ copies). The conjecture is that this holds for every $F$ except the four known exceptions $C_3\cup C_3$, $C_4\cup C_5$, $C_3\cup C_3\cup C_5$, $C_3\cup C_3\cup C_3\cup C_3$.

statement_sources.label: Glock, Joos, Kim, Kühn, Osthus, Resolution of the Oberwolfach problem (arXiv; J. Eur. Math. Soc.)
Lenz, Ringel, A brief review on Egmont Köhler's mathematical work, Discrete Math. (1991)

wpu-251.status_headline: Open in general. Settled for all sufficiently large n (Glock–Joos–Kim–Kühn–Osthus, JEMS), plus many cycle-type families and small orders.
wpu-251.verifier_checks: arXiv 1806.04644v2 abstract: decomposition for all large n only. Crossref confirms publication as J. Eur. Math. Soc. 23 (2021) 2511-2547, DOI 10.4171/JEMS/1060, so the venue 'to appear' was outdated and I updated it. Wikipedia raw text: all but finitely many instances are solved, all n<=60 are done, and four exceptions are known, which is consistent with 'open'. arXiv search (2026) shows only variant problems (honeymoon, directed). Category open is kept; the human-review flag on the 'Resolution' title is reasonable.

wpu-252.category_rationale: No resolution or claim found. Linear upper and lower bounds remain apart.
wpu-252.name: Maximum pathwidth of cubic graphs

partial_results.text: Every n-vertex cubic graph has pathwidth at most n/6 + o(n).
partial_results.title: Pathwidth of cubic graphs and exact algorithms

wpu-252.statement: Let $f(n)$ be the maximum pathwidth of an $n$-vertex cubic (3-regular) graph. Determine $f(n)$, or at least the constant $c=\lim f(n)/n$ if it exists. Fomin and Høie showed $f(n)\le n/6+o(n)$, and expander-type constructions give a linear lower bound, but the exact constant is unknown.

statement_sources.label: Fomin, Høie, Pathwidth of cubic graphs and exact algorithms, Inform. Process. Lett. (2006)

wpu-252.status_headline: Open. Upper bound n/6 + o(n) (Fomin–Høie 2006); the best linear lower bound is smaller and the exact growth is unknown.
wpu-252.verifier_checks: Spot-checked. Crossref confirms Fomin-Hoie (IPL 97, 2006). The Wikipedia Pathwidth text gives an n/6+o(n) upper bound against cubic graphs of pathwidth 0.082n, consistent with the headline. An arXiv 'pathwidth AND cubic' search finds nothing recent. Statement accurate, no copying.

wpu-253.category_rationale: Neither the graph reconstruction conjecture nor the new digraph reconstruction conjecture has been settled; 2026 arXiv work (a reduction, an expository survey) treats both as open.

evidence.note: Expository 2026 article surveying the conjecture as open and presenting an invariant-theoretic approach.
evidence.title: Shuffling the Deck: Invariant Theory and the Graph Reconstruction Conjecture

evidence.note: Claims a new reduction: the conjecture holds iff certain 2-connected graphs (domination number 2, or both G and complement of diameter 2) are reconstructible.
evidence.title: A Reduction of the Reconstruction Conjecture using Domination and Vertex Pair Parameters

wpu-253.name: Reconstruction conjecture (and the new digraph reconstruction conjecture)

partial_results.text: Trees on at least three vertices are reconstructible from their decks.
partial_results.title: Kelly: A congruence theorem for trees (1957)

partial_results.text: For almost all graphs, three suitably chosen cards already determine the graph, so almost all graphs are reconstructible.
partial_results.title: Bollobás: Almost every graph has reconstruction number three (1990)

wpu-253.review_reason: The bullet bundles two conjectures; the exact form of Ramachandran's degree-annotated digraph version (which degree data accompanies each card) should be checked against the 1981 paper.
wpu-253.statement: Kelly–Ulam reconstruction conjecture: any two finite simple graphs $G,H$ on $n\ge 3$ vertices whose decks agree (there is a bijection $\sigma:V(G)\to V(H)$ with $G-v\cong H-\sigma(v)$ for all $v$) are isomorphic. Ramachandran's new digraph reconstruction conjecture asks the analogous question for digraphs when each vertex-deleted subdigraph is supplied together with the in- and out-degree of the removed vertex (ordinary digraph reconstruction is known to fail).

statement_sources.label: Ramachandran, On a new digraph reconstruction conjecture, JCTB 31 (1981)
Schwenk, Some history on the reconstruction conjecture (JMM 2012 slides)

wpu-253.status_headline: Open. Proved for special classes (e.g., trees, almost all graphs); 2026 preprints give reductions and an invariant-theory survey but no resolution.
wpu-253.verifier_checks: Opened arXiv abs 2604.16567 (expository survey, 17 Apr 2026) and 2601.00620 (Aravind–Monikandan reduction, 2 Jan 2026) — notes match. Crossref-verified Ramachandran JCTB 31 (1981), Kelly PJM 1957, Bollobás JGT 1990. Degree data in the NDRC: secondary sources state the cards come with the (out-degree, in-degree) pair of the deleted vertex, consistent with the statement. arXiv 'reconstruction conjecture' search to Oct 2026 shows no proof/counterexample claims (2504.02353 interval graphs; 2608.22094 token-graph variant). No 8-word overlap.

wpu-254.category_rationale: Only dimensions up to 8 are settled exactly; for n=9 and beyond only lower bounds exist, which do not resolve the problem.

wpu-254.name: Snake-in-the-box problem

partial_results.text: An exhaustive computer search established the maximum snake length in dimension 8, completing exact values for all n ≤ 8.
partial_results.title: Östergård & Pettersson: Exhaustive search for snake-in-the-box codes

wpu-254.statement: For each $n$, determine $s(n)$, the maximum number of edges of an induced path (a 'snake') in the $n$-dimensional hypercube graph $Q_n$. Exact values are known only for $n\le 8$; the problem asks for $s(n)$ for all larger $n$ (and its asymptotic growth).

statement_sources.label: Orland et al., New Snake-in-the-Box Records via Snakepit Surgery and Learned Construction (arXiv 2026)

wpu-254.status_headline: Open. Optimal snake lengths are known through n = 8; a 2026 preprint reports a length-191 snake in Q_9 (previous record 190) plus new bounds for n = 10–13.
wpu-254.verifier_checks: Opened arXiv abs+HTML 2607.15270v3 (v3 30 Sep 2026): 191-snake in Q9 (previous 190), lower bounds n=10–13; 'Use of LLMs' section confirms LLM help with code/drafting (ai-assisted; records found by search, so no ai-partial). wpu-255.category_rationale: Proved only for sufficiently large n (non-explicit threshold); the statement for all n remains open. Large-n results and linear bounds are progress on a single statement, not a stated part.

wpu-255.name: Sumner's universal tournament conjecture

partial_results.text: The conjecture holds for all tournaments with n larger than some (very large) absolute constant.
partial_results.title: Kühn, Mycroft, Osthus (Proc. LMS 2011)

wpu-255.statement: Sumner's conjecture: for every $n\ge 2$, every tournament on $2n-2$ vertices contains a copy of every oriented tree on $n$ vertices.

statement_sources.label: Kühn, Mycroft, Osthus, A proof of Sumner's universal tournament conjecture for large tournaments, Proc. LMS (2011)

wpu-255.status_headline: Open. Proved for all sufficiently large n (Kühn–Mycroft–Osthus 2011); best uniform bound improved to ⌈(18n−23)/7⌉ in a 2026 preprint.
wpu-255.verifier_checks: Opened arXiv abs+HTML 2608.11667v1 (Ai–Lian, 12 Aug 2026): f(n) ≤ ⌈(18n−23)/7⌉ for all n ≥ 2, improving Dross–Havet; no AI disclosure. Crossref-verified Kühn–Mycroft–Osthus (Proc. LMS 102, 2011). arXiv search (Sumner/tournament/oriented tree) found no full claim. Statement exact (2n−2 vertices, every oriented n-vertex tree), no overlap with list text.

wpu-256.category_rationale: Verified computationally only for small dimensions (n ≤ 4); no claimed proof or counterexample found for general n.
wpu-256.name: Szymanski's conjecture

partial_results.text: Every permutation of the hypercube can be routed using two sets of arc-disjoint paths, i.e., the doubly directed hypercube is 2-rearrangeable.
partial_results.title: Gu & Tamaki (JPDC 1997)

wpu-256.statement: Let $\vec Q_n$ be the digraph obtained from the hypercube $Q_n$ by replacing each edge with two opposite arcs. Szymanski's conjecture: for every $n$ and every permutation $\pi$ of $V(Q_n)$ there are directed paths $P_v$ from $v$ to $\pi(v)$, one for each vertex $v$, that are pairwise arc-disjoint.

statement_sources.label: Gu & Tamaki, Routing a permutation in the hypercube by two sets of edge disjoint paths, J. Parallel Distrib. Comput. (1997)

wpu-256.status_headline: Open. Checked for n ≤ 4; Gu and Tamaki showed every permutation splits into two routable parts (2-rearrangeability).
wpu-256.verifier_checks: Spot-check: arXiv searches for Szymanski/hypercube routing return nothing recent; Wikipedia (lead only) reports verification for n ≤ 4 (Baudon–Fertin–Havel 2001), matching headline. Crossref-verified Gu–Tamaki JPDC 44 (1997) title. Statement (doubly directed Q_n, arc-disjoint paths for every permutation) accurate, no 8-word overlap.

wpu-257.category_rationale: Open; best accepted general bound is Haxell's 66/23. 2026 preprints claim improved constants and special classes but not the factor 2 for all graphs.

wpu-257.name: Tuza's conjecture

partial_results.text: Every graph satisfies τ(G) ≤ (66/23)ν(G).
partial_results.title: Haxell: Packing and covering triangles in graphs (Discrete Math. 1999)

partial_results.text: The conjecture holds asymptotically almost surely for Erdős–Rényi random graphs G(n,p).
partial_results.title: Kahn & Park: Tuza's conjecture for random graphs (RSA 2022)

wpu-257.statement: Tuza's conjecture: for every finite simple graph $G$, $\tau(G)\le 2\nu(G)$, where $\nu(G)$ is the maximum number of pairwise edge-disjoint triangles in $G$ and $\tau(G)$ is the minimum number of edges meeting every triangle of $G$.

statement_sources.label: Tuza, A conjecture on triangles of graphs, Graphs Combin. (1990)

wpu-257.status_headline: Open. Haxell's τ ≤ (66/23)ν stood since 1999; 2026 preprints claim 63/22 and 165/59 and the max-degree-≤7 case. None claims the full conjecture.
wpu-257.verifier_checks: Opened arXiv abs+HTML for 2609.13831v1 (Wang, 165/59, Lean-formalized; no AI disclosure found), 2608.23010v1 (Yi, 63/22; disclosure: developed without AI tools, LLMs for editing only), 2608.06538v1 (Gupta, Δ≤7; Claude Code and Codex used extensively, author selected arguments → ai-assisted, so no ai-partial badge). wpu-258.name: Unfriendly partition conjecture

partial_results.text: Graphs with only finitely many vertices of infinite degree have unfriendly partitions.
partial_results.title: Aharoni, Milner, Prikry: Unfriendly partitions of a graph (JCTB 1990)

partial_results.text: Every graph without a ray (one-way infinite path) has an unfriendly partition.
partial_results.title: Bruhn, Diestel, Georgakopoulos, Sprüssel: Every rayless graph has an unfriendly partition (Combinatorica 2010)

Aurichi & Real, Remarks on the countable case of the Unfriendly Partition Problem (arXiv 2024)

For $k=2$ this is Walecki's decomposition of $K_n$, $n$ odd.

wpu-273.statement: For an $r$-partite $r$-uniform hypergraph $H$ (vertex set split into $r$ classes, every edge meeting each class once), let $\nu(H)$ be the maximum matching size and $\tau(H)$ the minimum vertex-cover size. wpu-282.statement: Generalized regular expressions over a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ are built from $\emptyset$, $\{\varepsilon\}$ and single letters using union, concatenation, complement relative to $\Sigma^*$, and Kleene star; the star height of an expression is its maximal nesting depth of stars. Is there a constant $k$ such that every regular language over every finite alphabet is denoted by some generalized regular expression of star height at most $k$? (Sharper open forms ask whether $k=1$ suffices and whether the minimal generalized star height is computable.)

wpu-283.statement: Let $K$ be a number field with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. wpu-285.category_rationale: Shelah proved the main gap for countable first-order theories. The extensions listed (uncountable theories, AECs, $\aleph_1$-saturated models) have no accepted general resolution that we found.

wpu-285.review_reason: Collection entry stated only by example ('e.g.'). Some listed variants may already be partly settled (e.g. main-gap results for saturated models in Shelah's book, and AEC results). A specialist should confirm that none of the named variants is settled, since that would make the entry partial.
wpu-285.statement: For a complete first-order theory $T$ in a countable language, Shelah's main gap theorem gives a dichotomy: either $I(T,\aleph_\alpha)=2^{\aleph_\alpha}$ for every $\alpha>0$, or models of $T$ are determined by well-founded trees of dimension invariants and $I(T,\aleph_\alpha)<\beth_{\omega_1}(|\alpha|)$ for all $\alpha>0$. The open problem is to prove an analogous dichotomy in other settings, notably for first-order theories in uncountable languages, for abstract elementary classes, and for the $\aleph_1$-saturated models of a fixed countable theory.

statement_sources.label: Hart–Hrushovski–Laskowski, The uncountable spectra of countable theories, Annals of Math. (2000)

wpu-292.review_reason: The precise meaning of 'minimum universality spectrum' comes from the Džamonja/Shelah literature, which we could not open in full (paywalled). Check the statement wording against the source.
wpu-292.statement: For a complete first-order theory $T$, its universality spectrum records the cardinals $\lambda>|T|$ (and set-theoretic universes) in which $T$ has a universal model of size $\lambda$. Every $T$ has one when $\lambda^{<\lambda}=\lambda$. Is there a theory $T$ whose spectrum is minimum, i.e. one that provably has a universal model in $\lambda$ only when every theory does?
