wpu-305.statement: Let $(X_n)$ be a strictly stationary, centered, $\varphi$-mixing sequence of real random variables with $\mathbb{E}X_0^2<\infty$ and $\sigma_n^2=\operatorname{Var}(S_n)\to\infty$, where $S_n=X_1+\dots+X_n$. statement_sources.label: Adamczewski and Bugeaud, On the complexity of algebraic numbers I, Ann. of Math. 165 (2007)
Weisstein, MathWorld: Normal Number

wpu-338.status_headline: Open. No irrational algebraic number is known to be normal in any base; known results are complexity and digit-density lower bounds.

Crossref confirms Adamczewski-Bugeaud, Ann. of Math. 165 (2007) 547-565, and Bailey-Borwein-Crandall-Pomerance, JTNB 16 (2004) 487-518. Their described content matches the known theorems (superlinear complexity; at least about N^{1/D} ones among the first N binary digits). Statement correct, no overlap. The ambiguous-statement badge and review flag are reasonable. Open confirmed.

wpu-339.name: Is 10 a solitary number?
wpu-339.statement: Positive integers $m\neq n$ are friends if $\sigma(m)/m=\sigma(n)/n$, and $n$ is solitary if it has no friend. Does $10$ have a friend, i.e. is there a positive integer $m\neq10$ with $\sigma(m)/m=9/5$?

wpu-339.verifier_checks: Opened arXiv 0806.1001v2 (Ward, 6 Jun 2008): the evidence is accurate. SolitaryNumber.lean (is_ten_solitary) is research open. Statement correct (σ(10)/10=9/5). wpu-351.statement: Let $u_1=1$, $u_2=2$, and for $n\ge3$ let $u_n$ be the least integer greater than $u_{n-1}$ having exactly one representation $u_i+u_j$ with $i<j<n$ (Ulam's sequence $1,2,3,4,6,8,11,\dots$). Numerically the ratio is near $0.074$, but even positive upper density is unproved; Erdős asked whether the density is $0$.

wpu-355.statement: For the pairs $SO(n+1)\times SO(n)$, $U(n+1)\times U(n)$, $U(n)\times U(n)$ and $Sp(2n)\times Mp(2n)$ over a local field, the local conjecture states that in each generic Vogan $L$-packet exactly one representation admits a nonzero invariant Bessel or Fourier–Jacobi functional for the smaller group, and identifies it by a character built from local root numbers. Globally, a cuspidal representation has a nonvanishing period over the smaller group iff these local functionals exist everywhere and the central value $L(1/2)$ of the associated Rankin–Selberg type $L$-function is nonzero.

wpu-364.category_rationale: This is an open-ended characterization problem. Monogenity is decided field by field through index form equations, and there is a large 2025–2026 literature on families, but no general characterization exists.
wpu-364.name: Characterize number fields with a power integral basis
wpu-364.statement: Characterize the number fields $K$ that are monogenic, i.e. whose ring of integers is $\mathcal{O}_K=\mathbb{Z}[\alpha]$ for a single element $\alpha$, so that $1,\alpha,\dots,\alpha^{n-1}$ is an integral basis (Hasse's problem). Quadratic and cyclotomic fields are monogenic, but Dedekind exhibited a non-monogenic cubic field. No general criterion is known.

statement_sources.label: I. Gaál, Diophantine Equations and Power Integral Bases, 2nd ed. (Birkhäuser, 2019)

wpu-365.name: Beilinson's conjectures
wpu-365.statement: For a smooth projective variety $X$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ and integers $i,m$ (with $m$ outside the central range, $m>i/2+1$), Beilinson conjectured that the regulator from the integral part of motivic cohomology $H^{i+1}_{\mathcal M}(X,\mathbb{Q}(m))_{\mathbb Z}\otimes\mathbb{R}$ to real Deligne cohomology is an isomorphism, and that the leading coefficient of $L(h^i(X),s)$ at $s=m$ equals, up to a nonzero rational factor, the regulator determinant with respect to the natural $\mathbb Q$-structures (with analogous statements, involving heights, near the center).

statement_sources.label: Beilinson, Higher regulators and values of L-functions, J. Soviet Math. 30 (1985)

wpu-365.status_headline: Open in general; established only in special cases such as Dedekind zeta values (Borel) and some modular and CM cases. Active 2025–26 work on regulators, no full claim.

wpu-366.statement: Does there exist an absolute constant $c>0$ such that, for every primitive real (quadratic) Dirichlet character $\chi$ of conductor $q\ge 3$, the function $L(s,\chi)$ has no real zero $\beta$ with $1-c/\log q<\beta<1$? A real zero violating such a bound for some sequence of characters is called a Siegel (Landau–Siegel, exceptional) zero; the conjecture is that none exist.

wpu-367.statement: Let $\Phi(u)=\sum_{n\ge1}(2\pi^2n^4e^{9u}-3\pi n^2e^{5u})e^{-\pi n^2e^{4u}}$ and $H_t(x)=\int_0^\infty e^{tu^2}\Phi(u)\cos(xu)\,du$. The de Bruijn–Newman constant $\Lambda$ is the unique real number such that $H_t$ has only real zeros exactly when $t\ge\Lambda$. Determine $\Lambda$; since $\Lambda\ge0$ is known and RH is equivalent to $\Lambda\le0$, the question is whether $\Lambda=0$.

statement_sources.label: Rodgers–Tao, The De Bruijn–Newman constant is non-negative (Forum Math. Pi 2020)
Polymath, Effective approximation of heat flow evolution of the Riemann ξ function (Res. Math. Sci. 2019)

wpu-369.review_reason: Statement (2) is verified as Hardy–Littlewood's 1921 Theorem B (Math. Z. 10). Wikipedia frames these 'conjectures' as asking for the smallest admissible exponent, which is still open. Choose: keep solved for the two stated results (removed the trailing open-exponent sentence so statement and category agree), reframe as the open optimal-exponent question, or exclude as a misnomer.
wpu-369.statement: Let $N_0(T)$ be the number of zeros of odd order of $t\mapsto\zeta(\tfrac12+it)$ with $0<t\le T$. Show that (1) for every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large $T$, the interval $(T,T+T^{1/4+\varepsilon}]$ contains such a zero; and (2) for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $c>0$ such that $N_0(T+H)-N_0(T)\ge cH$ with $H=T^{1/2+\varepsilon}$ for all sufficiently large $T$.

statement_sources.label: Hardy–Littlewood, The zeros of Riemann's zeta-function on the critical line, Math. Z. 10 (1921)
Biao Wang, Simple critical zeros and distinct zeros of the Riemann zeta function in short intervals (arXiv 2026), historical introduction

wpu-370.statement: For fixed $k>-\tfrac12$, $\frac1T\int_0^T|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|^{2k}\,dt\sim a_k\,\frac{G(k+1)^2}{G(2k+1)}\,(\log T)^{k^2}$ as $T\to\infty$, where $G$ is the Barnes $G$-function and $a_k=\prod_p(1-p^{-1})^{k^2}\sum_{m\ge0}d_k(p^m)^2p^{-m}$ is the arithmetic factor (the random-matrix prediction for the moment constants).

wpu-371.name: Hilbert–Pólya conjecture
wpu-371.statement: Find a self-adjoint (possibly unbounded) operator $H$ on a Hilbert space whose spectrum, with multiplicity, is exactly the multiset of numbers $\gamma\in\mathbb C$ for which $\tfrac12+i\gamma$ is a nontrivial zero of $\zeta(s)$. Because self-adjoint operators have real spectrum, such an $H$ would force every nontrivial zero onto $\Re s=\tfrac12$; the conjecture asks for an operator of this kind, ideally of natural arithmetic, geometric or physical origin.

statement_sources.label: Connes, The Riemann Hypothesis: Past, Present and a Letter Through Time (arXiv 2026)

wpu-380.statement: For fixed $0<\alpha<\beta$, as $T\to\infty$, the number of pairs of ordinates $0<\gamma,\gamma'\le T$ of nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$ (counted with multiplicity) with $2\pi\alpha/\log T\le\gamma-\gamma'\le2\pi\beta/\log T$ is asymptotic to $N(T)\int_\alpha^\beta\big(1-(\tfrac{\sin\pi u}{\pi u})^2\big)du$, where $N(T)\sim\frac{T}{2\pi}\log T$; that is, normalized zero spacings have the GUE pair correlation.

wpu-381.statement: For $k\ge2$ write $\sum_{n\le x}d_k(n)=xP_k(\log x)+\Delta_k(x)$, where $d_k(n)$ counts ordered factorizations $n=n_1\cdots n_k$ and $P_k$ is a polynomial of degree $k-1$. Let $\alpha_k$ be the infimum of $a$ with $\Delta_k(x)\ll x^{a}$. Determine $\alpha_k$; the conjecture is $\alpha_k=\frac{k-1}{2k}$ for every $k\ge2$ (the lower bound $\alpha_k\ge\frac{k-1}{2k}$ is known).

wpu-388.statement: Let $V$ be a smooth Fano variety over a number field $K$ with $V(K)$ Zariski dense, and let $H$ be an anticanonical height. Manin's conjecture, in its current form, predicts a thin subset $Z\subset V(K)$ such that $\#\{x\in V(K)\setminus Z: H(x)\le B\}\sim c\,B(\log B)^{\rho-1}$ as $B\to\infty$, where $\rho$ is the rank of $\operatorname{Pic}V$ and $c>0$ is Peyre's constant. The original 1989 form removed only a proper Zariski-closed subset, and that form fails in general.

wpu-389.statement: Sato–Tate: for an elliptic curve $E/\mathbb{Q}$ without CM, write $a_p(E)=2\sqrt p\cos\theta_p$ with $\theta_p\in[0,\pi]$. Then the angles $\theta_p$ are equidistributed with respect to $\tfrac{2}{\pi}\sin^2\theta\,d\theta$. Generalizations predict equidistribution of normalized Frobenius conjugacy classes in a Sato–Tate group: for non-CM elliptic curves over arbitrary number fields, for abelian varieties and higher-genus curves (generically in $USp(2g)$), and for motives in general.

wpu-393.name: n conjecture
wpu-393.statement: Browkin–Brzeziński (1994): for each $n\ge3$ and $\epsilon>0$ there is a constant $C_{n,\epsilon}$ such that whenever integers $a_1,\dots,a_n$ satisfy $a_1+\dots+a_n=0$, $\gcd(a_1,\dots,a_n)=1$ and no proper subsum vanishes, $\max_i|a_i|<C_{n,\epsilon}\,\mathrm{rad}(a_1a_2\cdots a_n)^{2n-5+\epsilon}$. For $n=3$ this is the abc conjecture.

wpu-394.name: abc conjecture

partial_results.text: Stewart and Yu prove an unconditional bound of the form $\log c\ll\operatorname{rad}(abc)^{1/3+\varepsilon}$, still the best known type.

wpu-394.statement: For every $\epsilon>0$ there are only finitely many triples of coprime positive integers $a,b,c$ with $a+b=c$ and $c>\mathrm{rad}(abc)^{1+\epsilon}$, where $\mathrm{rad}(n)$ denotes the product of the distinct primes dividing $n$.

wpu-395.name: Szpiro's conjecture
wpu-395.statement: For every $\epsilon>0$ there is a constant $C(\epsilon)$ such that every elliptic curve $E$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ with minimal discriminant $\Delta_E$ and conductor $N_E$ satisfies $|\Delta_E|\le C(\epsilon)\,N_E^{6+\epsilon}$.

statement_sources.label: L. Szpiro, Discriminant et conducteur des courbes elliptiques, Astérisque 183 (1990), 7–18
H. Pasten, Improved bounds for Szpiro's conjecture (arXiv, 2026)

wpu-396.name: Zilber–Pink conjecture

partial_results.text: Habegger and Pila prove the conjecture for curves in abelian varieties defined over Q-bar, using o-minimal point counting.
partial_results.title: Curves in abelian varieties

wpu-396.statement: Let $V$ be an irreducible subvariety of $X$, where $X$ is a semiabelian variety or a mixed Shimura variety over $\mathbb{C}$. Call a subvariety $W\subseteq V$ atypical if it is an irreducible component of $V\cap S$ for some special subvariety $S\subseteq X$ with $\dim W>\dim V+\dim S-\dim X$. Conjecture (Zilber; Bombieri–Masser–Zannier; Pink): $V$ has just finitely many atypical subvarieties that are maximal for inclusion.

statement_sources.label: R. Pink, A combination of the conjectures of Mordell–Lang and André–Oort (Progress in Math. 235, 2005)
B. Zilber, Exponential sums equations and the Schanuel conjecture, J. London Math. Soc. (2002)

wpu-398.statement: Given a prime power $q$, a generator $g$ of the multiplicative group $\mathbb F_q^\times$ and an element $h\in\mathbb F_q^\times$, is there a classical (deterministic or randomized) algorithm that finds an integer $x$ with $g^x=h$ in time polynomial in $\log q$, uniformly over all finite fields? (More generally one asks this for other explicitly given cyclic groups.)

wpu-399.statement: For an elliptic curve $E$ over a finite field $\mathbb F_q$ and points $P,Q\in E(\mathbb F_q)$ with $Q\in\langle P\rangle$, is there a classical algorithm that finds $k$ with $Q=kP$ in sub-exponential time $\exp(o(\log q))$ for general curves (in particular for curves over prime fields $\mathbb F_p$)? Generic methods such as Pollard's rho need about $\sqrt{q}$ group operations.

wpu-400.name: Odd greedy expansion problem
wpu-400.statement: Let $x/y$ be a positive rational with $y$ odd. At each step subtract from the current remainder $r$ the unit fraction $1/d$ with $d$ the least odd integer satisfying $1/d\le r$. Does this odd greedy process reach remainder $0$ after finitely many steps for every such $x/y$, thereby expressing it as a finite sum of distinct unit fractions with odd denominators?

statement_sources.label: R. K. Guy, Unsolved Problems in Number Theory (Springer, 3rd ed. 2004), §D11
J. Louwsma, J. Martino, Rational numbers with odd greedy expansion of fixed length (arXiv 2309.07280)

Open consequences include the algebraic independence of $e$ and $\pi$ and the transcendence of $e+\pi$, $e\pi$, $\pi^e$, $\pi^\pi$ and $e^e$.

wpu-405.name: Which transcendental numbers are (exponential) periods?

partial_results.text: Periods are elementary computable, so a diagonal construction yields an explicit computable number that is not a period; Tent and Ziegler gave an independent short proof.
partial_results.title: Yoshinaga: computable non-periods (2008)

wpu-405.statement: A real number is a period in the sense of Kontsevich and Zagier if it equals an absolutely convergent integral $\int_\Delta R(x)\,dx$, where $R\in\mathbb Q(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ and $\Delta\subset\mathbb R^n$ is cut out by finitely many polynomial inequalities over $\mathbb Q$; a complex number counts when both its real part and its imaginary part do. Exponential periods also admit integrands $g\,e^{-f}$ with $f,g$ algebraic. Which transcendental numbers are (exponential) periods? In particular, are $e$, $1/\pi$ or Euler's $\gamma$ periods (conjecturally none is)?

statement_sources.label: M. Kontsevich, D. Zagier, Periods, in Mathematics Unlimited — 2001 and Beyond
M. Waldschmidt, Open Diophantine Problems (arXiv math/0312440)

wpu-406.statement: For real $x$ let $\mu(x)$ be the supremum of $\mu$ for which $0<|x-p/q|<q^{-\mu}$ has infinitely many rational solutions $p/q$. Roth's theorem gives $\mu(x)=2$ for all irrational algebraic $x$. Determine $\mu$ for specific transcendental or suspected-transcendental constants, notably whether $\mu(\pi)=2$ and, if $\gamma$ is irrational, the value of $\mu(\gamma)$; and more broadly understand the finer approximation of non-quadratic irrationals, e.g. whether every real algebraic number of degree $\ge3$ has unbounded continued-fraction partial quotients.

Which specific irrationals have this property? Numbers built for the purpose by prescribing their partial quotients are known to work, but the question is open for natural constants such as $\pi$, $\gamma$ and $\zeta(3)$ and for every real algebraic number of degree $\ge3$; it fails for $e$.

evidence.title: Real exponential sums over primes and prime gaps (arXiv:2307.08725v4)

wpu-423.name: Brocard's conjecture
wpu-423.review_reason: formal-conjectures (BrocardConjecture.lean @4c40439) marks the large-n variant 'research solved' citing Ferreira's unrefereed arXiv:2307.08725. Our assessment treats that claim as not accepted.
wpu-423.statement: Let $p_n$ be the $n$-th prime. Is it true that for every $n\ge2$ the open interval $(p_n^2,p_{n+1}^2)$ contains at least four primes? ($n=1$ is the exception, since only 5 and 7 lie between 4 and 9.)

statement_sources.label: Guy, Unsolved Problems in Number Theory, 3rd ed. (2004)
Formal Conjectures, Wikipedia/BrocardConjecture.lean

wpu-423.status_headline: Open. Follows from Oppermann's conjecture. An unrefereed preprint claims it only for large n, and formal-conjectures nonetheless tags that variant as solved.

wpu-424.category_rationale: Open for every polynomial of degree at least 2. Only almost-prime and two-variable analogues are known.
wpu-424.name: Bunyakovsky conjecture

partial_results.text: Every suitable irreducible quadratic polynomial, such as n^2+1, takes infinitely many values with at most two prime factors.
partial_results.title: Iwaniec (1978)

partial_results.text: The two-variable polynomial x^2+y^4 represents infinitely many primes, with the expected asymptotic.
partial_results.title: Friedlander–Iwaniec (1998)

partial_results.text: The binary cubic form x^3+2y^3 represents infinitely many primes.
partial_results.title: Heath-Brown (2001)

wpu-424.statement: Let $f\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ have degree at least 1 and positive leading coefficient. Suppose $f$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{Z}$ and $\gcd\{f(n):n\in\mathbb{N}\}=1$. Then $f(n)$ is prime for infinitely many positive integers $n$. Only the degree-one case (Dirichlet's theorem) is known; no polynomial of degree $\ge2$ is known to take infinitely many prime values.

statement_sources.label: Schinzel, Sierpiński, Sur certaines hypothèses concernant les nombres premiers, Acta Arith. 4 (1958)
Pintz, Landau's problems on primes, J. Théor. Nombres Bordeaux 21 (2009)

wpu-424.status_headline: Open. Not known for any polynomial of degree ≥ 2 (even n²+1). Known results concern almost primes and two-variable forms.
wpu-424.verifier_checks: Crossref confirms Schinzel-Sierpinski 1958, Pintz 2009, Iwaniec 1978, Friedlander-Iwaniec 1998 and Heath-Brown 2001 (Acta Math 186). arXiv search (Bunyakovsky, 2025-26) and the openai/math families index show no claim. Statement is correct, with no 8-word overlap with the list text. Open confirmed.

wpu-425.category_rationale: Primality of c_5 is undecided. It is far too large for primality tests, and trial division has found no small factor.
wpu-425.name: Catalan's Mersenne conjecture
wpu-425.statement: Define $c_0=2$ and $c_{k+1}=2^{c_k}-1$, giving $2,3,7,127,2^{127}-1,\ldots$. Are all the numbers $c_k$ prime? $c_0,\dots,c_4$ are prime and the primality of $c_5=2^{c_4}-1$ is unknown. Catalan's remark suggested they stay prime, but the expectation is that some $c_k$ is composite. Then every later term is composite too, since $2^m-1$ is composite for composite $m$.

statement_sources.label: Weisstein, Catalan-Mersenne Number, MathWorld
Formal Conjectures, Wikipedia/Mersenne.lean (catalans_mersenne_conjecture)

wpu-425.status_headline: Open. Whether c_5 = 2^(2^127−1)−1 is prime is unknown, and searches have found no small factor.
wpu-425.verifier_checks: Opened FC Wikipedia/Mersenne.lean at 4c40439: catalans_mersenne_conjecture asks whether all c_n with n>=5 are prime (answer left open), which matches the statement. The Wikipedia list phrases it as eventual compositeness, so the ambiguous-statement badge is justified. Definitions (c_0=2, c_{k+1}=2^{c_k}-1) are correct. Open confirmed.

wpu-426.category_rationale: Open for every k ≥ 2. Maynard–Tao sieve methods only give that some of the forms are simultaneously prime.
wpu-426.name: Dickson's conjecture

partial_results.text: For any admissible k-tuple of shifts n+h_i with k large in terms of m, at least m of the values are prime for infinitely many n.
partial_results.title: Maynard (2015)

partial_results.text: Extends the multiple-primes result to admissible tuples of general linear forms, including in subsets of the integers.
partial_results.title: Maynard (2016)

wpu-426.statement: Let $a_i+b_in$ ($1\le i\le k$) be linear forms with integers $a_i$ and $b_i\ge1$. Suppose that for every prime $q$ some $n$ makes $\prod_i(a_i+b_in)$ indivisible by $q$. Then for infinitely many positive integers $n$, all $k$ values $a_i+b_in$ are prime. The case $k=1$ is Dirichlet's theorem; the twin prime and Sophie Germain prime conjectures are special cases with $k=2$.

statement_sources.label: Schinzel, Sierpiński, Acta Arith. 4 (1958)
Hardy, Littlewood, Some problems of 'Partitio numerorum' III, Acta Math. 44 (1923)

wpu-426.status_headline: Open for k ≥ 2. Maynard–Tao methods show that, for admissible tuples with enough forms, some of them are simultaneously prime infinitely often.
wpu-426.verifier_checks: Crossref confirms Schinzel-Sierpinski 1958, Hardy-Littlewood 1923, Maynard 2015 (Annals) and Maynard 2016 (Compositio 152). The admissibility condition and conclusion are stated correctly. No overlap with the list text. No 2025-26 full claim found. OpenAI's 2026 DHL[40,2] claim is related but adds nothing beyond Maynard-type partial results here. Open confirmed.

wpu-427.category_rationale: Unproved, and it implies both the twin prime conjecture and (a strong form of) Goldbach's conjecture, so it is out of reach of current methods. It is supported only numerically.
wpu-427.name: Dubner's conjecture
wpu-427.statement: Call a prime a t-prime if $p-2$ or $p+2$ is also prime. Is every even integer $n>4208$ the sum of two t-primes? The conjecture strengthens Goldbach's conjecture and implies the twin prime conjecture.

statement_sources.label: Pandey, An intermediate conjecture between Goldbach and Dubner (arXiv:2608.02381v2, 2026)

wpu-427.status_headline: Open. Checked numerically to large bounds. A proof would imply the twin prime and binary Goldbach conjectures.
wpu-427.verifier_checks: Opened arXiv 2608.02381v2 (Pandey, v2 2026-08-26) abstract and HTML: it states Dubner's conjecture (every even n>4208 is a sum of two twin members; 33 exceptions up to 4208) and that it implies Goldbach and twin primes. The statement matches and is original. Pandey proves only a conditional density result. Open confirmed.

wpu-428.category_rationale: No unconditional level of distribution beyond 1/2 is known in this uniform form. Results past 1/2 hold only for restricted moduli or weights.
wpu-428.name: Elliott–Halberstam conjecture

partial_results.text: The estimate holds for every θ < 1/2.
partial_results.title: Bombieri (1965); A. I. Vinogradov (1965)

partial_results.text: Shows a weakened form beyond 1/2 for smooth moduli, enough to prove bounded gaps between primes.
partial_results.title: Zhang (2014)

partial_results.text: For a fixed residue class and well-factorable weights, primes are equidistributed to moduli beyond $x^{1/2}$.
partial_results.title: Maynard (2025)

wpu-428.statement: For every fixed $\theta<1$ and $A>0$, $\sum_{q\le x^{\theta}}\max_{(a,q)=1}\left|\pi(x;q,a)-\frac{\pi(x)}{\varphi(q)}\right|\ll_{\theta,A}\frac{x}{(\log x)^A}$. In other words, the primes have level of distribution $\theta$ for every $\theta<1$. The Bombieri–Vinogradov theorem gives this for $\theta<1/2$.

statement_sources.label: Bombieri, On the large sieve, Mathematika 12 (1965)
Maynard, Primes in arithmetic progressions to large moduli I, Mem. AMS (2025)

wpu-428.status_headline: Open. Proved only for θ < 1/2 (Bombieri–Vinogradov). Results beyond 1/2 need smooth moduli, fixed residues or well-factorable weights.
wpu-428.verifier_checks: Crossref confirms Bombieri 1965, Zhang 2014 and Maynard Mem. AMS 306 (2025). arXiv all-field search (Elliott-Halberstam, 2025-26) shows only variants and conditional work (Wright 2609.35950, Cantarini 2607.09110, Smith 2511.14810), no claim of EH. The formula is the standard one (the only overlap with the article is mathematical notation). Open confirmed.

wpu-429.name: Erdős–Mollin–Walsh conjecture
wpu-429.statement: Call $n$ powerful if $p^2\mid n$ for every prime $p\mid n$. Do there exist three consecutive positive integers $n,n+1,n+2$ that are all powerful? Erdős and, independently, Mollin and Walsh conjectured that no such triple exists. Four consecutive powerful numbers are impossible because one would be $\equiv2\pmod4$.

statement_sources.label: Mollin, Walsh, On powerful numbers, Int. J. Math. Math. Sci. 9 (1986)

partial_results.title: Stephens (1971)

wpu-430.statement: For distinct primes $p$ and $q$, is it true that $\frac{p^q-1}{p-1}$ never divides $\frac{q^p-1}{q-1}$? Feit and Thompson raised this because a proof would have shortened their proof of the odd order theorem.

statement_sources.label: Feit, Thompson, A solvability criterion for finite groups and some consequences, PNAS 48 (1962)
Stephens, On the Feit-Thompson conjecture, Math. Comp. 25 (1971)

wpu-431.category_rationale: Only verified numerically for many n. No proof or counterexample is known.
wpu-431.name: Fortune's conjecture
wpu-431.statement: For the primorial $p_n\#=\prod_{i\le n}p_i$, let $q_n$ be the smallest integer $m>1$ such that $p_n\#+m$ is prime (the $n$-th Fortunate number). Fortune's conjecture asserts that $q_n$ is prime for every $n$.

statement_sources.label: Golomb, The evidence for Fortune's conjecture, Math. Mag. 54 (1981)
Weisstein, Fortunate Prime, MathWorld

wpu-431.status_headline: Open. Checked for many n. Any composite Fortunate number would have to be at least the square of the next prime.
wpu-431.verifier_checks: Crossref confirms Golomb, Math. Mag. 54 (1981). Definition (least m>1 with p_n#+m prime) and conjecture are correct. The headline's claim that a composite Fortunate number is at least p_{n+1}^2 follows directly from the definition. arXiv search finds no claim. Open confirmed.

wpu-433.category_rationale: It is a statistical conjecture with empirical support only. Its predicted Mersenne-prime count differs from the Lenstra–Pomerance–Wagstaff heuristic, and neither is proved.
wpu-433.name: Gillies' conjecture
wpu-433.statement: Gillies (1964) proposed a statistical model for the prime factors of Mersenne numbers $M_p=2^p-1$ ($p$ prime): for $A<B\le\sqrt{M_p}$, as $B/A\to\infty$ and $M_p\to\infty$, the count of prime factors of $M_p$ lying in $[A,B]$ should be asymptotically Poisson with mean $\log\big(\log B/\log\max(A,2p)\big)$. A consequence is that roughly $\frac{2}{\log 2}\log\log x$ Mersenne primes lie below $x$.

statement_sources.label: Gillies, Three new Mersenne primes and a statistical theory, Math. Comp. 18 (1964)
Wagstaff, Divisors of Mersenne numbers, Math. Comp. 40 (1983)

wpu-433.status_headline: Open. A heuristic, statistical conjecture with some empirical support. Its predicted count of Mersenne primes differs from the Lenstra–Pomerance–Wagstaff heuristic.
wpu-433.verifier_checks: Crossref confirms Gillies 1964 and Wagstaff 1983. The statement was mathematically right but followed the Wikipedia sentence closely (a 7-word run 'the number of prime divisors of M ... in'), so it was rewritten in original form. The two cases are folded into max(A,2p). Open and ambiguous-statement (a heuristic, statistical conjecture) confirmed.

wpu-440.name: New Mersenne conjecture
wpu-440.statement: For an odd natural number $p$, consider three conditions: (a) $p$ has one of the forms $2^k\pm1$ or $4^k\pm3$ for some $k$; (b) $2^p-1$ is prime; (c) $(2^p+1)/3$ is prime. Bateman, Selfridge and Wagstaff conjectured that whenever two of these conditions hold, the third also holds.

statement_sources.label: Bateman, Selfridge, Wagstaff, The new Mersenne conjecture, Amer. Math. Monthly 96 (1989)
Formal Conjectures, Wikipedia/Mersenne.lean

wpu-440.status_headline: Open. Consistent with all known Mersenne and Wagstaff primes. Heuristics suggest only finitely many p meet two of the conditions.
wpu-440.verifier_checks: Crossref confirms Bateman-Selfridge-Wagstaff, Monthly 96 (1989). Opened FC Wikipedia/Mersenne.lean: IsSpecialForm and the new-Mersenne predicate match. The statement repeated the list text's 8-token run 'p = 2^k ± 1 or p = 4^k ± 3', so it was reworded. Open confirmed.

wpu-442.statement: Let $f_1,\ldots,f_k\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$ be irreducible, nonconstant, with positive leading coefficients. Suppose no prime $q$ divides $f_1(n)\cdots f_k(n)$ for every integer $n$. Then for infinitely many positive integers $n$, all of $f_1(n),\ldots,f_k(n)$ are prime. This generalizes both Dickson's and Bunyakovsky's conjectures.

wpu-443.statement: A Sierpiński number is an odd positive integer $k$ such that $k\cdot 2^n+1$ is composite for every $n\ge 1$. wpu-444.statement: Wolstenholme's theorem gives $\binom{2p-1}{p-1}\equiv 1 \pmod{p^3}$ for every prime $p\ge 5$. The conjectured converse (attributed to J. P. Jones) asserts that no composite $n$ satisfies $\binom{2n-1}{n-1}\equiv 1 \pmod{n^3}$, so that among integers $n\ge 2$ this congruence holds exactly for the primes $n\ge 5$.

wpu-444.status_headline: Open. No composite solution is known; McIntosh (1995) reported none below 10^9, and later work proves the converse only for special families of n.

wpu-481.review_reason: The reading decides the category. Universal reading ('for every admissible k,b,c, infinitely many primes?'): false by elementary or refereed counterexamples (78557·2^n+1 Sierpinski; 8^n+1 factors), so solved/S2. Per-triple reading: open for many triples, e.g. (k,b,c)=(1,2,-1) is the Mersenne prime question. The intended conjecture, with covering-set and algebraic-factor obstructions excluded, is also open. A reviewer may prefer open plus ambiguous-statement.
wpu-481.statement: For integers $k\ge1$, $b\ge2$, $c\ne0$ with $\gcd(k,c)=\gcd(b,c)=1$, let $a_n=(k\,b^n+c)/\gcd(k+c,b-1)$. Unless $(a_n)$ is ruled out by a covering set of primes or an algebraic factorization (e.g. $78557\cdot2^n+1$, $8^n+1$), are there infinitely many $n\ge1$ with $a_n$ prime? (Without that exclusion the list's literal wording is false.)

wpu-490.name: Woodin's Ω-conjecture

Kennard–Wu, Halperin's conjecture in formal dimensions up to 20 (arXiv 2104.04086v1)

wpu-499.status_headline: Open. Known for equal-rank homogeneous spaces (Shiga–Tezuka) and for formal dimension at most 20 (Kennard–Wu, Comm. Algebra 2023).
wpu-499.verifier_checks: Opened arXiv 2104.04086v1. Crossref shows it was published (Comm. Algebra 51(8), 2023, 3606-3622), so "claimed ... arXiv 2021 / preprint" was outdated; evidence, partial_results and headline updated. Crossref confirms Shiga-Tezuka, Ann. Inst. Fourier 37 (1987). arXiv title search shows no newer Halperin result. Open is right.

wpu-500.category_rationale: An openai/math manuscript (family 304, model-produced per the README) claims the conjecture in every finite dimension for Hausdorff, second-countable manifolds without boundary, which is the catalogued statement. No independent review or Lean proof.

evidence.note: Claims every locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group acting faithfully and continuously on a connected finite-dimensional manifold is Lie.
evidence.title: The Hilbert–Smith conjecture in every finite dimension

wpu-500.name: Hilbert–Smith conjecture

partial_results.text: Every locally compact group acting faithfully on a connected 3-manifold is a Lie group.
partial_results.title: Pardon (2013)

wpu-500.review_reason: Major AI proof claim without public expert assessment. Maps to Hilbert's fifth problem only as a related generalization, since the Gleason–Montgomery–Zippin solution of hilbert-05 does not settle Hilbert–Smith.
wpu-500.statement: If a locally compact topological group $G$ acts continuously and faithfully on a connected finite-dimensional topological manifold, must $G$ be a Lie group? By known reductions this is equivalent to: for no prime $p$ does the additive group $\mathbb{Z}_p$ of $p$-adic integers act faithfully on such a manifold.

statement_sources.label: Pardon, The Hilbert–Smith conjecture for three-manifolds, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 26 (2013)
formal-conjectures, HilbertProblems/5.lean

wpu-500.status_headline: Still listed as open. OpenAI's openai/math release (Oct 2026) claims a proof in every finite dimension; unreviewed, no Lean proof. Proved in dimension 3 (Pardon, 2013).
wpu-500.verifier_checks: Opened the pinned tree (HTTP 200), README (OpenAI, 23 Sep 2026) and CONTENTS.md family 304 (second-countable LC group, connected Hausdorff second-countable manifold without boundary). Second countability of G is no real restriction, since the standard reduction to Z_p actions makes this cover the catalogued conjecture. formal-conjectures HilbertProblems/5.lean at 4c40439 opened (category research open). Crossref confirms Pardon JAMS 26 (2013). maps_to hilbert-05 related is right (catalogue entry exists). A2 confirmed.

wpu-501.category_rationale: The finiteness-of-components conjecture is open with no known counterexample. Cornelissen–Zahidi note that some of Mazur's stronger conjectures had to be modified after a counterexample by Colliot-Thélène–Skorobogatov–Swinnerton-Dyer (1997). Which named conjecture that refutes could not be pinned down, so this is not classed partial.

evidence.note: Shows Mazur's finiteness conjecture implies no Diophantine model of ℤ in ℚ, and records that stronger Mazur conjectures needed modification.
evidence.title: Topology of Diophantine Sets: Remarks on Mazur's Conjectures

evidence.claimant: Jean-Louis Colliot-Thélène, Alexei Skorobogatov, Peter Swinnerton-Dyer
evidence.note: Cited by Cornelissen–Zahidi as a counterexample to some of Mazur's stronger conjectures. Its exact target was not verified from the paper itself.
evidence.title: Double fibres and double covers: paucity of rational points

wpu-501.name: Mazur's conjectures
wpu-501.review_reason: Collection entry: it is unclear which of Mazur's 1992 conjectures the CT–S–SD counterexample refutes; if it refutes a named conjecture of the 1992 paper, the entry could be 'partial' (P2). Not the same as Mazur's 'conjecture B' on uniform bounds (solved list), a false friend.
wpu-501.statement: Mazur's conjectures on the topology of rational points (1992): the central one asserts that for every variety $V$ over $\mathbb Q$, the closure of $V(\mathbb Q)$ in $V(\mathbb R)$ (Euclidean topology) has only finitely many connected components. Mazur also proposed stronger density statements and $p$-adic analogues. The finiteness conjecture would imply that $\mathbb Z$ admits no Diophantine model over $\mathbb Q$.

statement_sources.label: Mazur, The topology of rational points, Experiment. Math. 1 (1992)
Cornelissen–Zahidi, Topology of Diophantine sets: remarks on Mazur's conjectures (arXiv math/0006140)

wpu-501.status_headline: Open. The main finiteness conjecture is open; a 1997 counterexample (Colliot-Thélène–Skorobogatov–Swinnerton-Dyer) forced changes to some stronger versions.
wpu-501.verifier_checks: Opened arXiv math/0006140v1 and read its text: Conjecture 2.1 (Mazur Conj. 3, finiteness of real components) is called the weakest and has no known counterexample; Remark 2.3 says some stronger Mazur conjectures had to be slightly modified after the CT-S-SD counterexample. Crossref confirms CT-S-SD, Acta Arith. 79 (1997) 113-135, and Mazur, Exp. Math. 1 (1992). The Contemp. Math. 270 venue was not confirmed from the arXiv page. Open with low confidence and a review flag is appropriate, since which numbered conjecture CT-S-SD refutes (a possible P2) is unverified. No copying (max run 3).

wpu-502.category_rationale: Proved for many classes of groups but open in general. OpenAI's 2026 claims concern coarse assembly and Baum–Connes injectivity, and neither would disprove the Novikov conjecture.

evidence.note: Claims a bounded-geometry space whose coarse assembly map is not rationally injective. This is the coarse analogue, not the group-theoretic Novikov conjecture.
evidence.title: A counterexample to the coarse Novikov conjecture

evidence.note: Claims failure of rational injectivity of Baum–Connes assembly for some group. Injectivity would imply Novikov for that group, but its failure does not disprove Novikov.
evidence.title: A torsion-free counterexample to reduced Baum–Connes injectivity

wpu-502.name: Novikov conjecture

partial_results.text: The Novikov conjecture holds for all finitely generated groups of finite asymptotic dimension.
partial_results.title: Yu (1998)

wpu-502.statement: Let $G$ be a discrete group, $M$ a closed oriented smooth manifold and $f:M\to BG$ a continuous map. For $x\in H^*(BG;\mathbb Q)$ define the higher signature $\langle L(M)\cup f^*x,[M]\rangle$, where $L(M)$ is the Hirzebruch L-class. Novikov conjectured that, for every $G$ and $x$, these higher signatures are invariant under orientation-preserving homotopy equivalences $h:M'\to M$ (using $f\circ h$ on $M'$).

statement_sources.label: Yu, The Novikov conjecture for groups with finite asymptotic dimension, Ann. of Math. 147 (1998)

wpu-502.status_headline: Open. Proved for large classes of groups (e.g. finite asymptotic dimension, Yu 1998). OpenAI's Oct 2026 assembly-map counterexample claims are related but do not decide it.
wpu-502.verifier_checks: Opened both pinned trees (coarse Novikov, family 307; BC injectivity, family 285) and the CONTENTS.md descriptions. Logic checked: failure of (coarse or reduced) rational injectivity of assembly does not disprove the Novikov higher-signature conjecture, so open is right and the AI claims are related only. Crossref confirms Yu, Annals 147 (1998).

wpu-503.category_rationale: No proof or counterexample found; only the tame case (at least one quadrisecant) is known.
wpu-503.name: Quadrisecants of wild knots

partial_results.text: Every nontrivial tame knot or nonsplit link in $\mathbb R^3$ has a quadrisecant.
partial_results.title: Kuperberg (1994)

wpu-503.statement: A quadrisecant of a knot $K\subset\mathbb R^3$ is a straight line meeting $K$ in four distinct points. Kuperberg proved that every nontrivial tame knot has at least one quadrisecant. Does every wild knot (a topologically embedded circle not isotopic to a polygonal knot) have infinitely many quadrisecants?

statement_sources.label: Kuperberg, Quadrisecants of knots and links, J. Knot Theory Ramifications 3 (1994)

wpu-503.status_headline: Open. Every nontrivial tame knot has a quadrisecant (Kuperberg, 1994); infinitely many for wild knots is conjectured.
wpu-503.verifier_checks: Spot-check: arXiv title search "quadrisecant" shows nothing after 2016 and no claim; nothing in the openai/math CONTENTS. Crossref confirms Kuperberg, JKTR 3 (1994). Statement accurate.

wpu-504.category_rationale: Disproved at every prime for all heights $\ge2$ by Burklund–Hahn–Levy–Schlank (2023). No journal version was found, but the result is treated as settled by independent experts: Ravenel, who posed the conjecture, calls it its resolution in a 2026 expository paper. The 2024 Oberwolfach Arbeitsgemeinschaft on the disproof (organized by the authors) shows wide engagement.

evidence.claimant: Robert Burklund, Jeremy Hahn, Ishan Levy, Tomer M. Schlank
evidence.note: Shows that the T(n+1)-localized algebraic K-theory of BP⟨n⟩^{hℤ} is not K(n+1)-local, so the two localizations differ at every prime for heights ≥ 2.
evidence.title: K-theoretic counterexamples to Ravenel's telescope conjecture

evidence.note: Report of a 2024 Oberwolfach Arbeitsgemeinschaft on the disproof, organized by the four authors themselves; shows broad engagement but is neither refereed nor an independent check.
evidence.title: Arbeitsgemeinschaft: Algebraic K-Theory and the Telescope Conjecture

evidence.note: Expository companion paper by the conjecture's originator, describing the BHLS work as the recent resolution of the telescope conjecture.
evidence.title: Cyclotomic extensions in stable homotopy theory

wpu-504.name: Telescope conjecture
wpu-504.review_reason: Classed solved on expert acceptance (S2) rather than a refereed journal version, which was not found.
wpu-504.statement: Ravenel's telescope conjecture: for every prime $p$ and every height $n\ge0$, if $F$ is a finite $p$-local spectrum of type $n$ with a $v_n$-self map $v$, is the telescope $v^{-1}F$ equivalent to the $K(n)$-localization $L_{K(n)}F$? Equivalently, does telescopic localization $L_{T(n)}$ agree with $K(n)$-localization?

statement_sources.label: Burklund–Hahn–Levy–Schlank, K-theoretic counterexamples to Ravenel's telescope conjecture (arXiv 2310.17459v1)

wpu-504.status_headline: Solved (negatively). Burklund–Hahn–Levy–Schlank (2023) showed telescopic and K(n)-localizations differ at every prime for heights ≥ 2; widely accepted, journal version not found.
wpu-504.verifier_checks: Opened arXiv 2310.17459v1 (BHLS; heights >=2 at every prime), arXiv 2606.08166v2 (Ravenel expository paper; abstract calls BHLS "the recent resolution of the telescope conjecture"), Crossref for 10.4171/owr/2024/47 (authors/organizers are BHLS themselves; OWR is a workshop report, not refereed). No journal version was found via Crossref. Solved (S2) is kept, resting on independent expert treatment (Ravenel) and wide acceptance. Corrected the OWR item, which was marked "refereed" and called independent acceptance.

wpu-505.category_rationale: Unknot recognition is known to lie in NP ∩ co-NP, but no polynomial-time algorithm is known or claimed.

evidence.note: New hierarchy-based algorithm for incompressibility and unknot detection; not claimed to run in polynomial time.
evidence.title: Incompressible surfaces, hierarchies and unknot recognition

wpu-505.name: Unknotting problem

partial_results.text: Unknot recognition is in NP.
partial_results.title: Hass–Lagarias–Pippenger (1999)

partial_results.text: Unknot recognition is in co-NP (unconditionally).
partial_results.title: Lackenby (2021)

wpu-505.statement: Is there an algorithm that decides whether a given knot diagram represents the unknot in time polynomial in the number of crossings of the diagram?

statement_sources.label: Hass–Lagarias–Pippenger, The computational complexity of knot and link problems, J. ACM 46 (1999)
Lackenby, The efficient certification of knottedness and Thurston norm, Adv. Math. 387 (2021)

wpu-505.status_headline: Open. Unknot recognition is in NP (Hass–Lagarias–Pippenger) and co-NP (Lackenby); no polynomial-time algorithm is known.
wpu-505.verifier_checks: Opened arXiv 2607.23350v1 (Lackenby, 25 Jul 2026; new hierarchy algorithm, with no polynomial-time claim). Crossref confirms Hass-Lagarias-Pippenger JACM 46 (1999) and Lackenby Adv. Math. 387 (2021). Spot-check searches found no polynomial-time claim. Open is right.

wpu-506.category_rationale: Verified only for specific knots and families; open in general, with no claimed full proof.
wpu-506.name: Volume conjecture
wpu-506.statement: Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture: for a knot $K\subset S^3$ let $J_N(K;q)$ be its $N$-colored Jones polynomial, normalized so the unknot gives 1. Does $\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{2\pi}{N}\log|J_N(K;e^{2\pi i/N})|=v_3\,\|S^3\setminus K\|$, where $\|\cdot\|$ is simplicial volume and $v_3$ the volume of the regular ideal tetrahedron? For hyperbolic $K$ the right side is the hyperbolic volume of the complement.

statement_sources.label: Murakami–Murakami, The colored Jones polynomials and the simplicial volume of a knot, Acta Math. 186 (2001)

wpu-506.status_headline: Open. Verified for specific knots such as the figure-eight and some families; open for general knots.
wpu-506.verifier_checks: Spot-check: arXiv title search "volume conjecture" (2025-2026) shows only special cases and variants (Chen-Yang/Turaev-Viro fillings, figure-eight, Andersen-Kashaev for 42,000 knots); no general claim, and none in the openai/math CONTENTS. Crossref confirms Murakami-Murakami, Acta 186 (2001). Statement formula accurate (7-token overlap is formula symbols only).

wpu-507.category_rationale: No claimed proof or counterexample. Bestvina–Brady showed that this conjecture and the Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture cannot both hold. OpenAI's claimed Eilenberg–Ganea counterexample (Oct 2026), even if correct, does not decide Whitehead.

evidence.note: Shows that either the Whitehead conjecture or the Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture is false.
evidence.title: Morse theory and finiteness properties of groups

evidence.note: Claims a group of cohomological dimension 2 and geometric dimension 3. This concerns the companion conjecture and does not resolve Whitehead's.
evidence.title: A finitely generated counterexample to the Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture

wpu-507.name: Whitehead conjecture
wpu-507.statement: Whitehead's asphericity conjecture (1941): if $K$ is an aspherical 2-dimensional CW complex, meaning $\pi_2(K)=0$ so that its universal cover is contractible, is every connected subcomplex of $K$ also aspherical?

statement_sources.label: Bestvina–Brady, Morse theory and finiteness properties of groups, Invent. Math. 129 (1997)

wpu-507.status_headline: Open. OpenAI's Oct 2026 claim of an Eilenberg–Ganea counterexample is related through Bestvina–Brady but does not settle the Whitehead conjecture.
wpu-507.verifier_checks: Opened the pinned Eilenberg-Ganea tree (HTTP 200), README and CONTENTS.md family 249 (cd 2, gd 3, finitely generated). Crossref confirms Bestvina-Brady, Invent. Math. 129 (1997). Logic checked: Bestvina-Brady only says that at least one of Whitehead and Eilenberg-Ganea fails, so an EG counterexample leaves Whitehead undecided; open is right. maps_to kourovka-17-086 related matches curated coverage. Statement accurate (shared run with list text 4 words).

wpu-508.category_rationale: Open in general; known reductions and special cases do not settle it. No full claim was found.

evidence.note: Claims that Zeeman's conjecture for standard polyhedra implies it in general.

wpu-508.name: Zeeman conjecture

partial_results.text: For standard spines of 3-manifolds, the Zeeman conjecture is equivalent to the Poincaré conjecture.
partial_results.title: Gillman–Rolfsen (1983)

wpu-508.statement: Zeeman's collapsibility conjecture: if $K$ is a finite contractible 2-dimensional polyhedron (or CW complex), is $K\times[0,1]$ collapsible, possibly after subdivision? The conjecture implies both the 3-dimensional Poincaré conjecture and the Andrews–Curtis conjecture.

statement_sources.label: Gillman–Rolfsen, The Zeeman conjecture for standard spines is equivalent to the Poincaré conjecture, Topology 22 (1983)

wpu-508.status_headline: Open. Gillman–Rolfsen (1983) tied the case of standard spines to the Poincaré conjecture; an Aug 2026 preprint (Dynnikov) reduces the general case to standard polyhedra.
wpu-508.verifier_checks: Opened arXiv 2608.23331v1 (Dynnikov, 24 Aug 2026: Zeeman for standard polyhedra implies it in general). Crossref confirms Gillman-Rolfsen, Topology 22 (1983). arXiv title search shows no full claim. Open is right; note that with Perelman, Gillman-Rolfsen settles standard spines of 3-manifolds, but not all standard polyhedra.

wpu-509.category_rationale: An openai/math manuscript (family 340, model-produced per the README) claims a closed exact Lagrangian in $T^*(S^9\times S^{N-1})$ (for some large even $N$) that is diffeomorphic to the base but not Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section. That would be a full negative answer. Not reviewed, no Lean proof.

evidence.title: A counterexample to the nearby Lagrangian conjecture

wpu-509.name: Nearby Lagrangian conjecture

partial_results.text: For any closed exact Lagrangian in $T^*N$, projection to $N$ is a simple homotopy equivalence.

partial_results.text: The conjecture holds for $T^*T^2$.
partial_results.title: Dimitroglou Rizell–Goodman–Ivrii (2016)

wpu-509.statement: Let $N$ be a closed smooth manifold and $L\subset T^*N$ a closed exact Lagrangian submanifold of its cotangent bundle with the canonical symplectic form. Must $L$ be Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section?

statement_sources.label: Abouzaid–Kragh, Simple homotopy equivalence of nearby Lagrangians, Acta Math. 220 (2018)

wpu-509.verifier_checks: Opened the pinned tree (HTTP 200), README (OpenAI, 23 Sep 2026) and CONTENTS.md family 340: a closed exact Lagrangian in T*(S^9 x S^{N-1}) diffeomorphic to the base but not Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section. method: Researched 2026-10-11 by AI research agents from primary sources (papers, source-of-record pages, repositories) under fixed category rules, then checked by independent adversarial verifier agents that opened the cited evidence. Items marked needs_human_review are judgment calls. An independent integrity audit (every link checked, a random sample and every decision re-checked against primary sources) corrected 203 entries on 2026-10-11.
